faqs.question: Is teaching experience gained from private schools or private colleges acceptable for Principal/Vice Principal positions?
faqs.answer:
Private School Experience: Yes, provided the experience is from a recognized school and satisfies the experience requirement mentioned in the notification.

Private College Experience: Generally No. The notification specifically requires teaching experience in recognized schools (as Vice Principal/PGT/TGT), not colleges or universities. Experience from colleges usually does not substitute for the required school teaching experience unless UPSC specifically clarifies otherwise.

faqs.question: Does experience as an Assistant Professor in a college or university qualify towards the required experience for Principal or Vice Principal?
faqs.answer:
No, in most cases. The notification requires experience as:
- Principal: 10 years as Vice Principal/PGT/TGT in a recognized school.
- Vice Principal: 2 years as PGT or 3 years as TGT in a recognized school.

Assistant Professor experience in colleges or universities is not listed as eligible experience.

faqs.question: Can a candidate apply for both Principal and Vice Principal posts simultaneously, and will there be a single combined exam or separate exams?
faqs.answer:
Yes. If you independently satisfy the eligibility criteria for both posts, you may apply for both (subject to UPSC application rules).

UPSC has scheduled a Combined Recruitment Test (CRT) for this recruitment. The CRT is planned for 1 November 2026, after which shortlisted candidates will be called for interviews. UPSC will issue detailed instructions regarding the examination arrangement.

faqs.question: Can candidates without any teaching or administrative experience apply for these vacancies?
faqs.answer:
No. Experience is mandatory:
- Principal: 10 years teaching experience.
- Vice Principal: 2 years as PGT or 3 years as TGT.

Fresh graduates or candidates without the prescribed experience are not eligible.

faqs.question: Are candidates currently in the final year (appearing) of their B.Ed degree eligible to apply?
faqs.answer: No. Candidates must possess the required B.Ed qualification on or before the closing date of applications. Final-year or appearing candidates who have not yet obtained the degree are not eligible unless UPSC specifically provides an exception in the notification.

faqs.question: Is teaching experience acquired while simultaneously completing a PG (e.g., M.Sc.) degree counted as valid experience?
faqs.answer:
It may be counted, provided:
- You had already acquired the minimum qualification required to hold that teaching post,
- The teaching appointment was regular/valid,
- The experience certificate is issued by the employer, and
- The experience meets UPSC's eligibility conditions.

However, if the teaching experience was obtained before becoming eligible for the teaching post or during an internship/training period, it may not be accepted. UPSC verifies such cases during document scrutiny.

faqs.question: What is the maximum age limit for Vice Principal, and can candidates over 35 years of age apply?
faqs.answer:
Vice Principal Upper Age Limits:
- UR / EWS: 35 years
- OBC: 38 years
- SC / ST: 40 years
- Additional relaxations are available for eligible categories such as PwBD as per Government rules.

So yes, candidates above 35 years can apply if they are eligible for age relaxation under the applicable reservation category.

faqs.question: Where can candidates access and download the official notification document?
faqs.answer: Candidates should download the official notification directly from the official UPSC Website (upsc.gov.in) or the UPSC Online Recruitment Application (ORA) Portal (upsconline.nic.in).

faqs.question: Is there negative marking in the recruitment exam?
faqs.answer: Yes. UPSC's Combined Recruitment Test (CRT) generally follows the Commission's standard objective-type pattern, where negative marking of one-third (1/3) of the marks assigned to a question is applied for each incorrect answer, unless the detailed exam notice specifies otherwise. Candidates should verify the detailed examination scheme released by UPSC before the exam.

faqs.question: Are contractual PGT teachers, state government teachers (e.g., Grade 3/L-2, BPSC PGTs), or specific diploma/degree holders (e.g., BFA/TGT Drawing) eligible?
faqs.answer:
Eligibility depends on whether the candidate satisfies all conditions in the notification:
- State Government PGT/TGT Teachers: Generally eligible if they hold the prescribed educational qualifications and required teaching experience in a recognized school.
- Contractual PGT/TGT Teachers: Contractual experience may be accepted if it is recognized by UPSC, supported by valid experience certificates, and meets the notification's requirements.
- BPSC PGT / Other State PGTs: Eligible if their service is equivalent to the prescribed PGT/TGT experience in a recognized school.
- BFA / TGT Drawing or Other Specialized Teachers: Eligible only if they possess the required Master's Degree, B.Ed., and prescribed PGT/TGT experience. Merely holding a BFA or working as a Drawing Teacher does not automatically satisfy the eligibility conditions.

overview: All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi has published official Notice No. 103/2026 dated 24.07.2026 for conducting the Nursing Officer Recruitment Common Eligibility Test (NORCET)-11 for direct recruitment to the post of Nursing Officer (Group-B) at Level 07 in the Pay Matrix.

This prestigious national-level recruitment exam is conducted for filling 2218+ tentative vacancies across 19 AIIMS institutes (Avantipora, Bathinda, Bhopal, Bilaspur, Bhubaneswar, Deoghar, Gorakhpur, Guwahati, Kalyani, Mangalagiri, Nagpur, New Delhi, Patna, Rae Bareli, Raipur, Rishikesh, Vijaypur Jammu, Rewari), CAPFIMS Maidangarhi, ESIC Hospitals, NITRD, CIP Ranchi, and Central Government Hospitals in New Delhi (Safdarjung Hospital, Dr. RML Hospital, Lady Hardinge Medical College / Kalawati Saran Children's Hospital, and RHPT Nazafgarh).

Pay Level 07 in 7th CPC Pay Matrix offers a starting Basic Pay of Rs. 44,900/- (pre-revised PB-2 Rs. 9,300–34,800 with Grade Pay of Rs. 4,600/-) with gross monthly salary ranging between Rs. 75,000 to Rs. 85,000/- including DA, HRA, Nursing Allowance, Dress Allowance, and Transport Allowance.

As per the 4th Central Institute Body (CIB) decision dated 27.07.2019, 80% of total advertised vacancies across participating AIIMS institutes are reserved for Female candidates and 20% for Male candidates.

Eligible candidates holding B.Sc. (Hons) Nursing / B.Sc. Nursing / Post-Basic B.Sc. Nursing (Freshers eligible, NO experience required) OR Diploma in General Nursing Midwifery (GNM) with mandatory 2 years' experience in a minimum 50-bedded hospital after acquiring qualification and nursing registration, aged between 18 to 30 years as on 13.08.2026, can apply online at www.aiimsexams.ac.in from 24th July 2026 to 13th August 2026 (up to 5:00 PM).

education: CATEGORY A (B.Sc Nursing Graduates - NO Experience Required):

• B.Sc. (Hons.) Nursing / B.Sc. Nursing from an Indian Nursing Council (INC) or State Nursing Council recognized Institute / University OR B.Sc. (Post-Certificate) / Post-Basic B.Sc. Nursing from an INC/State Nursing Council recognized Institute.
• Registration: Mandatory active registration as Nurse & Midwife with State Nursing Council or Indian Nursing Council (INC).
• Experience: NIL (0 Years experience required - Fresh graduates can apply immediately).
CATEGORY B (GNM Diploma Holders - MANDATORY 2 Years' Experience):
• Diploma in General Nursing Midwifery (GNM) from an INC or State Nursing Council recognized Board / Council / Institute.
• Registration: Mandatory active registration as Nurse & Midwife with State Nursing Council or Indian Nursing Council (INC).
• Experience: Two (2) Years' Experience in a MINIMUM 50-bedded Hospital after acquiring the educational qualification and after obtaining Council Registration.

selectionProcess.description: Qualifying CBT examination of 90 minutes duration consisting of 100 MCQs (100 Marks). Divided into 20 MCQs on General Knowledge & Aptitude and 80 MCQs on Nursing Courses. The test contains 5 sections of 18 minutes duration each (20 questions per section). Sequential auto-submission applies and candidates cannot revisit completed sections. Negative marking of 1/3rd (0.33) mark for each wrong answer. Qualifying marks: 50 percentile for UR/EWS, 45 percentile for OBC, 40 percentile for SC/ST (5% additional relaxation for PwBD). Candidates qualifying Stage I equal to 5 times the total vacancies in each category will be called for Stage II Mains.

Final merit-ranking CBT examination of 180 minutes duration consisting of 160 MCQs (160 Marks). Entire exam focuses on Nursing courses with case scenario-based MCQs testing practical clinical competence and skills. Contains 4 sections of 45 minutes duration each (40 questions per section). Sequential auto-submission applies. Negative marking of 1/3rd mark for each wrong answer. Qualifying marks: 50% for UR/EWS, 45% for OBC, 40% for SC/ST (5% additional relaxation for PwBD). Final merit list for seat allocation is prepared solely based on Stage-II Mains performance.

howToApply: Step 1: Visit the official AIIMS examination website at www.aiimsexams.ac.in.
Step 2: On the home page, click on "Recruitment" and select "Nursing Officer Recruitment Common Eligibility Test (NORCET-11)".

Step 3: Click on "New Registration" if registering for the first time, or "Applicant Login" if you already possess a Registration ID from previous NORCET exams (OTR rule: Do NOT create a duplicate ID).
Step 4: Enter basic personal details, valid mobile number, email ID, educational qualifications, State/INC nursing registration details, and 2-year hospital experience (for GNM diploma holders).
Step 5: Upload scanned photograph, signature, and left thumb impression strictly adhering to prescribed specifications (clear background, correct pixel dimensions).
Step 6: Pay the online application fee (Rs. 3000 for UR/OBC, Rs. 2400 for SC/ST/EWS) using Debit Card, Credit Card, or Net Banking.
Step 7: Choose 3 preferred examination cities in order of preference.
Step 8: Review all details carefully on the preview screen and click "Final Submit". Print and safely store the generated Registration Slip for document verification.

OBC-NCL VALIDITY WINDOW: OBC certificates MUST be issued on or after 01.04.2026 up to 13.08.2026 for FY 2026-2027 based on FY 2025-2026 income.

SECTIONAL TIME LOCK: Both Stage I and Stage II exams feature sequential section locks. You have 18 minutes per section in Stage 1 and 45 minutes per section in Stage 2. Once a section timer expires, it auto-submits and you CANNOT go back to previous sections.

faqs.question: What is the official notice number and release date for AIIMS NORCET-11 2026?
faqs.answer: The official notice number is Notice No. 103/2026, released on 24th July 2026 by AIIMS New Delhi Examination Section.

faqs.question: What is the starting and closing date for AIIMS NORCET-11 online registration?
faqs.answer: Online registration starts on 24th July 2026 and closes on 13th August 2026 at 5:00 PM.

faqs.question: When will the Stage-I Prelims and Stage-II Mains CBT examinations be held?
faqs.answer: Stage-I NORCET Preliminary CBT is scheduled for Saturday, 12th September 2026. Stage-II NORCET Main CBT is scheduled for Wednesday, 30th September 2026.

faqs.question: How many total vacancies are advertised for AIIMS NORCET-11?
faqs.answer: A total of 2218+ tentative vacancies have been reported across 19 AIIMS institutes, CAPFIMS Maidangarhi, ESIC, NITRD, CIP Ranchi, and Central Government Hospitals in New Delhi.

faqs.question: What is the Pay Level and monthly starting salary for Nursing Officer in AIIMS?
faqs.answer: The post carries Pay Level 07 in the 7th CPC Pay Matrix (pre-revised PB-2 Rs. 9,300–34,800 + GP Rs. 4,600) with a starting basic pay of Rs. 44,900/- per month. Gross starting salary ranges between Rs. 75,000 to Rs. 85,000/- including DA, HRA, Nursing Allowance, and Uniform Allowance.

faqs.question: Is work experience mandatory for B.Sc. Nursing candidates?
faqs.answer: NO. B.Sc. (Hons) Nursing, B.Sc. Nursing, and Post-Basic B.Sc. Nursing graduates require ZERO years of experience. Fresh graduates with valid State/INC nursing registration are 100% eligible.

faqs.question: What are the experience requirements for GNM diploma holders in NORCET-11?
faqs.answer: GNM diploma candidates must have MANDATORY 2 Years' Experience in a minimum 50-bedded Hospital. The experience must be acquired AFTER acquiring the GNM qualification and obtaining State/INC nursing council registration.

faqs.question: What is the age limit for AIIMS NORCET-11 recruitment?
faqs.answer: Candidates must be between 18 to 30 years of age as on the closing date, 13th August 2026. Upper age relaxation applies for SC/ST (+5 yrs), OBC (+3 yrs), PwBD (+10 to 15 yrs), and Ex-Servicemen.

faqs.question: What is the 80:20 gender reservation rule in AIIMS NORCET?
faqs.answer: As per the 4th Central Institute Body (CIB) decision dated 27.07.2019, 80% of total advertised seats in AIIMS institutes are reserved for female candidates and 20% for male candidates.

faqs.question: What is the application fee for General, OBC, SC, ST, EWS, and PwBD candidates?
faqs.answer: General/OBC candidates pay Rs. 3000/-. SC/ST/EWS candidates pay Rs. 2400/-. PwBD candidates are exempted from fee (Rs. 0/-).

faqs.question: Is the application fee refundable for SC and ST candidates?
faqs.answer: YES. SC and ST candidates who appear in the Stage-I / Stage-II CBT examination will receive a 100% refund of Rs. 2,400/- back to their original payment account after result declaration and certificate verification.

faqs.question: What is the exam pattern for NORCET-11 Stage-I Preliminary CBT?
faqs.answer: Stage-I CBT lasts 90 minutes and consists of 100 MCQs (100 Marks): 20 MCQs on General Knowledge & Aptitude and 80 MCQs on Nursing subjects. It contains 5 sections of 18 minutes duration each (20 questions per section).

faqs.question: What is the exam pattern for NORCET-11 Stage-II Main CBT?
faqs.answer: Stage-II CBT lasts 180 minutes and consists of 160 MCQs (160 Marks) focusing on clinical case scenarios and practical nursing skills. It contains 4 sections of 45 minutes duration each (40 questions per section).

faqs.question: Is there negative marking in NORCET-11 exams?
faqs.answer: YES. There is a negative marking of 1/3rd (0.33) mark for every wrong answer in both Stage-I Prelims and Stage-II Mains CBT examinations.

faqs.question: How many candidates will be qualified in Stage-I to appear in Stage-II Mains?
faqs.answer: Candidates equal to 5 times the total advertised vacancies in each category (UR, OBC, SC, ST, EWS) along with all tie cases and PwBD qualified candidates will be shortlisted for Stage-II Mains.

faqs.question: Are Stage-I Prelims marks added to the final merit list?
faqs.answer: NO. Stage-I Prelims is purely qualifying in nature to shortlist candidates for Stage-II. The final merit list for institute allocation is prepared solely on the basis of marks obtained in Stage-II Mains.

faqs.question: What are the qualifying marks/percentiles for Stage-I and Stage-II?
faqs.answer: UR/EWS: 50%, OBC: 45%, SC/ST: 40%. PwBD candidates receive an additional 5% relaxation across all categories (UR-PwBD: 45%, OBC-PwBD: 40%, SC/ST-PwBD: 35%).

faqs.question: What is the issue date requirement for OBC-NCL category certificates?
faqs.answer: OBC-NCL certificates MUST be issued on or after 01.04.2026 up to 13.08.2026 for Financial Year 2026-2027 based on FY 2025-2026 income in the prescribed Central Government format.

faqs.question: What is the issue date requirement for EWS category certificates?
faqs.answer: EWS certificates MUST be issued on or after 01.04.2026 up to 13.08.2026 for Financial Year 2026-2027 based on FY 2025-2026 income.

faqs.question: What are the tie-breaking rules if two candidates score equal marks in Stage-II Mains?
faqs.answer: Tie-breaking sequence: 1) Fewer negative marks in Stage II Mains, 2) Higher score in Stage I Prelims, 3) Fewer negative marks in Stage I Prelims, 4) Older candidate by Date of Birth, 5) Alphabetical order of candidate name.

faqs.question: How does online choice filling and seat allocation work for AIIMS NORCET?
faqs.answer: After Stage II results, qualified candidates log in to exercise preference choices for participating AIIMS. Seat allocation occurs in a single general round based strictly on Stage II merit position and candidate preferences.

faqs.question: Is there any waiting list in AIIMS NORCET recruitment?
faqs.answer: NO. AIIMS New Delhi does NOT maintain any waiting list or reserve list for NORCET. Unallocated seats are carried forward to the next NORCET session.

faqs.question: Are government or PSU employees required to submit an NOC?
faqs.answer: YES. Candidates currently working in regular service in Central/State Govt, PSU, or Autonomous bodies must upload a No Objection Certificate (NOC) by 18th August 2026 (5:00 PM).

faqs.question: Can selected candidates request inter-AIIMS mutual transfers later?
faqs.answer: Inter-AIIMS transfers are governed by individual AIIMS cadre rules and Central Institute Body policies. Generally, direct transfers are restricted during initial probation periods.

faqs.question: What is the promotion hierarchy for Nursing Officers in AIIMS?
faqs.answer: Nursing Officer (Level 7) ➔ Senior Nursing Officer (Level 8) ➔ Assistant Nursing Superintendent (Level 10) ➔ Deputy Nursing Superintendent (Level 11) ➔ Nursing Superintendent (Level 12) ➔ Chief Nursing Officer (Level 13).

faqs.question: Are candidates with B.Sc Post-Basic eligible without hospital experience?
faqs.answer: YES. Post-Basic B.Sc. Nursing graduates are treated at par with B.Sc. Nursing graduates and require ZERO years of hospital experience.

faqs.question: What happens if a candidate submits multiple or duplicate application forms?
faqs.answer: Submitting duplicate applications under multiple IDs is strictly forbidden. AIIMS software will flag duplicate registrations, leading to immediate cancellation of all applications without fee refund.

faqs.question: Can GNM experience gained during internship or training be counted?
faqs.answer: NO. The 2-year hospital experience for GNM candidates MUST be completed AFTER the declaration of final examination results and AFTER obtaining State/INC nursing council registration.

faqs.question: What is the minimum bed strength requirement for GNM hospital experience?
faqs.answer: The experience must be from a hospital with a minimum bed strength of 50 beds during the candidate's tenure of employment.

faqs.question: What are the photo and signature upload requirements for NORCET-11?
faqs.answer: Photo must be recent color with white background (50-100 KB, JPG format). Signature must be in running hand with black ink on white paper (20-50 KB). Left thumb impression must be clear without smudging (20-50 KB).

faqs.question: When will the Admit Cards for Stage-I CBT be available for download?
faqs.answer: Stage-I Admit Cards will be uploaded on the AIIMS portal www.aiimsexams.ac.in on 09th September 2026.

faqs.question: How can candidates check their application acceptance or rejection status?
faqs.answer: Application status will be uploaded on candidate login dashboards on 24th August 2026. Any deficiencies must be rectified during the correction window.

faqs.question: Are scribe facilities provided for PwBD candidates?
faqs.answer: YES. PwBD candidates with benchmark disability >=40% in visual or physical impairment preventing writing can opt for a scribe and get 20 minutes/hour compensatory time upon producing valid medical certificates.

faqs.question: Is there any normalization procedure used if Stage I or II is conducted in multiple shifts?
faqs.answer: YES. As per AIIMS Notice No. 35/2023, standard percentile normalization methodology is used to equate difficulty levels across different shifts.

faqs.question: Which Central Government hospitals in Delhi are participating in NORCET-11?
faqs.answer: Safdarjung Hospital (SJH), Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital, Kalawati Saran Children's Hospital (KSCH), and Rural Health Training Centre (RHPT) Nazafgarh.

faqs.question: What is the cadre posting rule for CAPFIMS Maidangarhi?
faqs.answer: CAPFIMS Maidangarhi is an independent medical institute. Nursing staff selected for CAPFIMS will be posted exclusively at CAPFIMS and cannot seek transfer to AIIMS New Delhi.

faqs.question: Is there any bond or probation period for AIIMS Nursing Officers?
faqs.answer: Newly appointed Nursing Officers undergo a standard 2-year probation period. Joining conditions are specified in the appointment letter issued by the allocated institute.

faqs.question: What is the helpline or official contact email for AIIMS NORCET queries?
faqs.answer: Candidates can contact the AIIMS Examination Section via email at norcet-exam@aiimsexams.ac.in or call toll-free helpline 1800117898.

faqs.question: Can male candidates apply for AIIMS NORCET-11?
faqs.answer: YES. Male candidates are eligible and compete for 20% of the total advertised vacancies across AIIMS institutes, as well as unreserved seats in non-AIIMS hospitals.

faqs.question: What documents are required during physical document verification?
faqs.answer: Registration slip, admit card, 10th certificate, B.Sc/GNM degree/diploma, marks sheets, council registration, 2-year experience certificate (for GNM), caste/EWS certificate, NOC, and photo ID proof.

faqs.question: What should a candidate do if there is a spelling mistake in their name or father's name?
faqs.answer: Corrections can be made during the editing window (14th to 16th August 2026). Minor discrepancies can be supported by a legal affidavit during document verification.

faqs.question: Is hostel accommodation provided for AIIMS Nursing Officers?
faqs.answer: Hostel accommodation is subject to availability at the allocated AIIMS campus. If hostel is not available or opted out, House Rent Allowance (HRA) is paid as per Central Govt rules.

faqs.question: How are exam cities assigned if preferred city choices are filled?
faqs.answer: Cities are allotted on a first-come, first-served basis during registration. If preferred choices are full, AIIMS assigns the nearest available city in the same or adjacent state.

faqs.question: Where can I download the official AIIMS NORCET-11 Notification PDF?
faqs.answer: The official notification PDF (Notice No. 103/2026) can be downloaded directly from www.aiimsexams.ac.in under the "Recruitment" tab.

faqs.question: What is the educational qualification required for Assistant/UDC posts?

faqs.question: Can a final year student apply for this recruitment?
faqs.answer: No, graduation must be completed with a minimum of 60% marks or 6.32 CGPA as of the application submission date.

faqs.question: Is there any skill test in the selection process?
faqs.answer: Yes. Qualified candidates from the written test will undergo a Skill Test in Computer Literacy (for Assistant/UDC) or English Stenography (for JPA/Stenographer), which is of qualifying nature.

overview: The Ministry of Railways, Railway Recruitment Boards (RRB) has released the Centralized Employment Notification (CEN) No. 03/2026 for the recruitment of Section Controllers across various Zonal Railways.
Eligible Indian Nationals and other specified nationals can apply online for a total of 119 vacancies. This is a Level 6 graduate-level post offering an initial pay of Rs. 35,400.

Candidates must carefully read the detailed instructions regarding eligibility, medical standards (A-2), exam pattern, and the application process before submitting their online forms. Candidates who have undergone Lasik surgery are strictly not eligible for this post.

Visual Acuity: Distant Vision: 6/9, 6/9 without glasses (No fogging test). Near Vision: Sn 0.6, 0.6 without glasses.
Must pass test for Colour Vision, Binocular Vision, Night Vision, and Myopic vision.
CRITICAL: Candidates who have undergone Lasik Surgery or any other surgical procedure to correct refractive error are NOT eligible for the post of Section Controller.

selectionProcess.stage: Stage 1: Single Stage Computer Based Test (CBT)
selectionProcess.description: Screening exam consisting of 100 questions to be solved in 120 minutes. There is a negative marking of 1/3 for each incorrect answer.
Candidates equal to 8 times the vacancies will be shortlisted. Candidates need a minimum T-Score of 42 marks in each test battery to qualify. No negative marking.
Candidates equal to the number of vacancies (1:1 ratio) will be called for DV based on combined merit (70% CBT + 30% CBAT weightage).
Selected candidates will undergo a strict A-2 medical fitness test by Railway Medical Authorities.

examPattern.negativeMarking: 1/3 mark deducted for each wrong answer in CBT.

topics: Mathematics: Number System, Ratio & Proportions, Averages, Percentages, Profit, Loss & Discounts, Time, Speed, Distance, Power & Work, Algebra, Linear Equations, Arithmetic Progression, LCM, HCF, Geometry, Area & Volumes, Probability and Statistics (Basic Level).

Data Analysis & Interpretation: Multi-source Data Analysis - Examination, analysis and Inference drawing from text, tabular data and data represented graphically (charts, graphs, scatter plot, pie chart, statistical curve distribution, Venn Diagrams). Data Sufficiency, Data Arrangement.
Logical Reasoning: Binary Logic, Syllogism, Clocks & Calendars, Assumptions, Blood Relations, Family Tree, Solving logic-based puzzles.

Reading Comprehension: Passages and Questions in English language from History, Society, Literature, Science, Environment, Abstract, Mythology, Technology and Culture. Focus on Main idea, Supporting idea, Application, Logical Structure & Style.
Analogy - Identifying relationship between two items and applying it to another pair.
Series Completion - Identifying the pattern in a sequence of numbers and predicting the next term.
Solving Coding-Decoding type questions.
Solving Ranking and Arrangements based problems.

howToApply: Step 1: Visit the official RRB website and navigate to the CEN 03/2026 application link.
Step 2: Create an Account using a valid mobile number and email ID. Identity authentication via Digi Locker or Aadhaar is highly recommended.
Step 3: Log in and fill the ONLINE application form. Choose your preferred RRB zone and the medium of examination carefully (no changes allowed later).
Step 4: Pay the application fee online using internet banking, debit/credit cards, or UPI.
Step 5: Capture a Live Photograph using a webcam/mobile camera. Ensure a neutral expression, plain background, and no accessories like caps or glasses.
Step 6: Upload scanned mandatory documents like your signature and SC/ST certificate (if claiming free travel pass).
Step 7: Verify all details and submit the application before the closing date of 14.08.2026.
documentsRequired: Live Photograph (captured via webcam during application).
Candidate Signature: Scanned in JPG/JPEG format (30 KB to 49 KB), signed in running handwriting using a black ink pen on white paper.
SC/ST Certificate (if applicable): Scanned in PDF format (less than 400 KB) to claim the Free Train Travel Pass.
Aadhaar Card (for identity authentication).
EBC Certificate / BPL Card / Izzat MST (if claiming Economically Backward Class fee concession).
OBC-NCL / EWS Certificates (as per prescribed annexures) to be produced during Document Verification.
importantInstructions: Banned Items: Mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, calculators, smartwatches, and metallic accessories are strictly prohibited inside the examination hall.
Single Application: Submit only one application for one RRB. Multiple applications will lead to summary rejection and debarment.
Lasik Surgery: Candidates who have undergone Lasik surgery are strictly NOT eligible for the Section Controller post.
Signature Guidelines: Signatures in BLOCK, CAPITAL, or DISJOINED letters will lead to application rejection.
Modification Window: Corrections can be made from 17.08.2026 to 26.08.2026 by paying a Rs. 250/- modification fee per occasion. Chosen RRB and Account creation details cannot be modified.
Account Creation: If you have already created an account for RRB CENs in 2024, 2025, or 2026, you must use the same credentials to apply.

faqs.question: What is the last date to apply for RRB Section Controller 2026?
faqs.answer: The last date to submit the online application is 14th August 2026 (23:59 Hrs).

faqs.question: What is the age limit for RRB Section Controller?
faqs.answer: The age limit is 20 to 33 years as on 01.07.2026. Age relaxations are applicable for SC, ST, OBC-NCL, ExSM, and PwBD candidates as per rules.

faqs.question: Is Lasik surgery allowed for RRB Section Controller?
faqs.answer: No, candidates who have undergone Lasik surgery or any other corrective refractive surgery are NOT eligible, as the required medical standard is A-2.

faqs.question: What is the application fee for RRB CEN 03/2026?
faqs.answer: The application fee is Rs. 500/- for General/OBC candidates and Rs. 250/- for SC/ST/Female/ExSM/EBC/PwBD candidates. A partial or full refund is provided upon appearing for the CBT.

faqs.question: Can I apply to multiple RRB zones?
faqs.answer: No, candidates can apply to only ONE RRB. Applying to multiple RRBs will lead to rejection of all applications and debarment.

faqs.question: What is the selection process for Section Controller?
faqs.answer: The selection process includes a Single Stage Computer Based Test (CBT), Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT), Document Verification (DV), and Medical Examination (A-2).

faqs.question: Is there a negative marking in the RRB CBT exam?
faqs.answer: Yes, 1/3rd of the marks allotted for a question will be deducted for each incorrect answer in the CBT.

overview: The 130 Infantry Battalion (Territorial Army) Ecological, KUMAON has officially announced a massive recruitment rally for the year 2026, offering 69 crucial vacancies for dedicated professionals. This open recruitment rally is scheduled to be held at the prominent Devkaliya Ground, Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand from 03 August 2026 to 08 August 2026. This prestigious rally represents a major rehabilitation opportunity specifically targeting Ex-servicemen of the Indian Armed Forces and Ex-women employees of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF & CC) as well as the State Forest Department (SFD).

The vacancies are distributed across several technical and non-technical trades under the Soldier category, including 49 posts for Soldier (General Duty), which are reserved for eligible candidates from the state of Uttarakhand. The remaining 20 posts span diverse trades such as Chef Community, Washer Man, Tailor, Equipment Repairer, Hair Dresser, Black Smith, Clerk, Carpenter, and House Keeper. These trade vacancies are open to eligible candidates from all over India on an All India Basis. The notification highlights that candidates must meet precise service, character, and medical guidelines to be eligible for selection.

Eligible candidates are required to register online at the official portal www.130ta.com. The registration site provides details regarding eligibility criteria, medical standards, and detailed terms of engagement. In cases where candidates face technical or connectivity issues preventing online registration, they can directly report to the recruitment rally site on 03 August 2026 starting at 06:00 Hrs with all their original documents, certificates, and photographs. indian-army-officer-entries-2026.jobLocation: Anywhere in India (Subject to service requirements)
overview: The Indian Army has officially released the recruitment notification for the JAG Entry Scheme 125th Course commencing in April 2027. This prestigious scheme offers a direct pathway for unmarried male and unmarried female law graduates to serve as commissioned officers in the Judge Advocate General (JAG) Branch of the Indian Army, which functions as the legal department of the military.

Under this entry, selected candidates will be granted a Short Service Commission (SSC) in the regular Army for a tenure of up to 14 years. Training for the course will be conducted for a duration of 49 weeks at the esteemed Officers Training Academy (OTA) in Chennai. Crucially, candidates must possess a minimum of 55% aggregate marks in their LLB degree and must have appeared for the CLAT PG 2026 examination (conducted in December 2025).

The online registration process opens on 17 July 2026 at 15:00 hours and will conclude on 17 August 2026 at 15:00 hours. The selection process involves initial shortlisting based on CLAT PG scores, followed by a rigorous 5-day Service Selection Board (SSB) Interview at Prayagraj, Bhopal, Bengaluru, or Jalandhar, and a subsequent medical examination. Successful candidates will be commissioned as Lieutenants with an attractive salary package of approximately 17-18 Lakhs CTC per annum, along with numerous military allowances.

Candidates must be eligible for registration as an advocate with the Bar Council of India/State Bar Council.
Candidate must have obtained their LLB degree from a College/University recognized by the Bar Council of India.

Only candidates holding their LLB Degree and Marksheet are eligible to apply; candidates appearing in the final year of LLB who do not have their degree/marksheet on application submission date are NOT eligible.

The detailed medical standards and procedures are published on the official portal www.joinindianarmy.nic.in.

SSB Medical Examination: Recommended candidates after Stage-II of the SSB interview will undergo a comprehensive medical examination by the Armed Forces Medical Board (SMB/AMB/RMB). The validity of the medical examination is 270 days.

selectionProcess.description: The Integrated HQ of MoD (Army) reserves the right to shortlist candidates based on their CLAT PG 2026 scores without assigning any reason. The shortlisting is done based on the vacancy-to-call-up ratio.

selectionProcess.stage: Stage 2: SSB Centre and Date Selection
selectionProcess.description: Shortlisted candidates must log in to the portal and select their SSB Centre and Date on a "First Come First Serve" basis. This option is open for two weeks in September. Selected centre/dates cannot be changed later.

Shortlisted eligible candidates will undergo a 5-day SSB selection procedure at one of the Selection Centres: Prayagraj (UP), Bhopal (MP), Bengaluru (Karnataka), or Jalandhar (Punjab). The SSB interview is conducted in two stages. Those who clear Stage-I proceed to Stage-II, while failed candidates are returned on the first day.
Candidates recommended by the SSB will undergo a medical examination conducted by the Armed Forces Medical Board (SMB/AMB/RMB) to verify physical and medical fitness.

A final merit list is prepared on the basis of marks obtained by the candidates in the SSB Interview. In case of equal marks, the older candidate is placed higher. If marks and age are both equal, the candidate with higher percentage in the qualifying exam (LLB) is placed higher.
Joining letters for Pre-Commission training at OTA Chennai will be issued in order of merit among medically fit candidates, subject to the availability of vacancies.

examPattern.negativeMarking: No written test is conducted. Selection is directly via SSB Interview Stage-I & Stage-II evaluations.

sections.name: SSB Stage-II (Psychological Tests, GTO Tasks & Personal Interview)

topics: Officer Intelligence Rating (OIR) Tests (Verbal and Non-verbal reasoning).
Picture Perception and Discussion Test (PPDT) including story writing, individual narration, and group discussion.
Thematic Apperception Test (TAT) - project story writing based on series of pictures.
Word Association Test (WAT) - sentence formulation with provided words.
Situation Reaction Test (SRT) - written responses to real-life everyday scenarios.
Self Description (SD) - writing self-evaluation and opinion of family, friends, and teachers.
Group Discussion (GD) on social and current affairs.
Group Planning Exercise (GPE) - collaborative tactical planning.
Progressive Group Task (PGT) & Half Group Task (HGT) - obstacle-crossing teamwork.
Command Task (CT) - leadership evaluation in an obstacle scenario.
Individual Obstacles (IO) - physical agility and stamina tasks.
Group Obstacle Race / Snake Race - competitive team obstacle navigation.
Final Group Task (FGT) - final team-based obstacle task.
Personal Interview with the Interviewing Officer (covering candidate bio-data, education, sports, career, general awareness, and legal principles).
Board Conference on Day 5: Final review and confirmation of recommendation decision by the entire board.

howToApply: Step 1: Open the official recruitment portal of the Indian Army: www.joinindianarmy.nic.in.
Step 2: Solve the Captcha to enter the website, then click on the 'Officer Entry Appln/Login' button.

Step 3: Click on the 'Registration' button (if not already registered). Fill in the online registration form carefully with your basic personal details. Registrations are not required if already registered.
Step 4: Once registered, login with your credentials and click on 'Apply Online' under your Candidate Dashboard.
Step 5: A page titled 'Officers Selection - Eligibility' will open. Locate the 'Short Service Commission JAG Entry Course' and click on the 'Apply' button next to it.
Step 6: Read the application instructions thoroughly. Click 'Continue' to move to the 'Application Form' page.

Step 7: Complete the online form across the various segments: Personal Information, Communication Details, Education Details, and Details of Previous SSB Interviews. Click 'Save & Continue' after completing each segment.
Step 8: After completing the final segment, you will see the 'Summary of your information' page. Carefully verify and edit any incorrect entries.
Step 9: Click the 'Submit' button to complete your application. You must click 'Submit' every time you edit your details before the closing date.

Step 10: Retain two printouts of your online application form with the auto-generated Roll Number. This printout will be available 30 minutes after the final closure of the online application on the last day.
documentsRequired: One printout copy of the online application form, duly signed, with a self-attested passport size photograph affixed.

Original and self-attested photocopy of Matriculation/Secondary School Examination Certificate or equivalent issued by the concerned Board of Education as proof of date of birth, candidate's name, and parents' names.
Original and self-attested photocopy of 12th Class Certificate & Marks sheet.

Original and self-attested photocopy of Graduation Degree/Provisional Degree (In case of three years LLB after graduation) issued by a recognized university. Provisional Degree must not be more than six months old as of 01 April 2027 (issued between 01 October 2026 and 01 April 2027).

Original and self-attested photocopy of LLB Degree/Provisional Degree issued by a recognized university. Provisional Degree must not be more than six months old as of 01 April 2027 (issued between 01 October 2026 and 01 April 2027).
Self-attested photocopies of Marks sheets of all years/semesters of the LLB course, along with the originals.

Original and photocopy of Registration with the Bar Council of India/State Bar Council, OR a Certificate from the College/University confirming that the LLB course in the said institution is recognized by the Bar Council of India.
Original Certificate issued by the University stating the exact formula used for conversion of CGPA/Grades into percentage of marks.
Original and self-attested copy of CLAT PG 2026 Score Card (conducted in December 2025).

Armed Forces serving candidates: A written intimation to their Commanding Officer stating that they have applied for this exam. The application must be countersigned by the CO at the time of the SSB interview.
importantInstructions: RED ALERT: No offline applications! There is absolutely no provision for submitting offline or physical applications. Do not send any hard copies of your application to the Headquarters.
RED ALERT: DIGILOCKER Certificates will NOT be accepted at the Selection Centre in lieu of original certificates. Candidates must bring physical original certificates for verification.

WARNING: Any discrepancy in candidate's name, parent's name, or date of birth between the matriculation certificate and the online application profile will lead to immediate cancellation of candidature.

WARNING: Candidates must have their CLAT PG 2026 results verified at the Selection Centre before the SSB interview begins. Any candidate who fails or is unwilling to get their result verified will be declared ineligible, and their candidature will be cancelled immediately.

WARNING: Marriage Restrictions: Candidates are not permitted to marry during their training period. Candidates must not marry until they complete the full 49-week training at OTA Chennai. If a candidate marries after the application date or during training, they will be withdrawn and must refund all training costs incurred.

INFORMATION: Training Cost Liability: The entire training cost is at government expense. faqs.question: What is the official title of this recruitment course?
faqs.answer: The recruitment course is officially titled "JAG Entry Scheme 125th Course (April 2027) : Short Service Commission (NT) Course for Law Graduates (Men & Women)".

faqs.question: How many vacancies are advertised under this course?
faqs.answer: There are a total of 10 combined vacancies for men and women announced for this course.

faqs.question: What is the nature of the commission offered for this entry?
faqs.answer: Selected candidates are granted a Short Service Commission (SSC) in the regular Indian Army for an initial period of 10 years, which is extendable by a further period of 4 years, making a total tenure of up to 14 years.

faqs.question: What is the gender and marital status eligibility for the JAG 125th entry?
faqs.answer: Only unmarried male and unmarried female law graduates are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: What are the age limit criteria for candidates?
faqs.answer: Candidates must be between 21 to 27 years of age as of 01 January 2027. They must have been born not earlier than 02 January 2000 and not later than 01 January 2006 (both dates inclusive).

faqs.question: Which document is accepted as proof of date of birth?
faqs.answer: The Matriculation/Secondary School Examination Certificate or an equivalent certificate issued by the concerned Board of Education is the only document accepted as proof of date of birth, candidate's name, and parents' names.

faqs.question: What are the minimum educational qualifications required to apply?
faqs.answer: Candidates must possess a minimum of 55% aggregate marks in their LLB Degree (either a 3-year professional course after graduation or a 5-year integrated course after 10+2). They must be eligible for registration as an advocate with the Bar Council of India or a State Bar Council, and must have graduated from a recognized college/university.

faqs.question: Is the CLAT PG score mandatory for this recruitment?
faqs.answer: Yes, appearing in the CLAT PG 2026 examination (conducted in December 2025) is mandatory for all candidates (including LLM qualified and LLM appearing candidates). No other CLAT PG score will be accepted.

faqs.question: Can candidates currently in the final year of their LLB course apply?
faqs.answer: No. Only candidates who already hold their LLB Degree and Marksheet are eligible to apply, provided they meet all other qualifications.

faqs.question: Where is the CLAT PG 2026 score verified?
faqs.answer: Candidates must get their CLAT PG 2026 results verified at the Selection Centre prior to the conduct of the SSB interview. If they fail or are unwilling to verify, their candidature will be cancelled.

faqs.question: Is there any provision for submitting offline or physical applications?
faqs.answer: No, applications are accepted strictly online. There is absolutely no provision for offline application submission, and the Directorate General of Recruiting will not accept any offline forms.

faqs.question: What is the application fee for the JAG 125th Entry Course?
faqs.answer: There is no application fee. The recruitment process is entirely transparent and free of cost for all categories.

faqs.question: Where can candidates submit their online applications?
faqs.answer: Applications must be submitted exclusively on the official recruitment website of the Indian Army: www.joinindianarmy.nic.in.

faqs.question: What are the online application opening and closing dates?
faqs.answer: The online application system opens on 17 July 2026 at 15:00 hours and closes on 17 August 2026 at 15:00 hours.

faqs.question: What are the physical testing standards for Officer Cadets before joining?
faqs.answer: The minimum physical standards candidates must acquire are: (i) 2.4 Km Run: 10 mins 30 secs for Men and 13 mins for Women; (ii) Push-ups: 40 for Men and 15 for Women; (iii) Pull-ups: 6 for Men and 2 for Women; (iv) Sit-ups: 30 for Men and 25 for Women; (v) Squats: 2 sets of 30 reps; (vi) Lunges: 2 sets of 10 reps on each leg; (vii) Swimming: Should know the fundamentals of swimming.

faqs.question: Where does the pre-commission training take place, and how long is it?
faqs.answer: The Pre-Commission training is conducted at the Officers Training Academy (OTA) in Chennai and lasts for a duration of 49 weeks starting in April 2027.

faqs.question: What qualifications are awarded after successful completion of training at OTA?
faqs.answer: All candidates who successfully complete the Pre-Commission training will be awarded a "Post Graduate Diploma in Defence Management and Strategic Studies" by the University of Madras.

faqs.question: What rank is awarded upon successful completion of training?
faqs.answer: On successful commissioning, candidates are appointed to the rank of Lieutenant.

faqs.question: What is the starting pay scale and salary structure for a Lieutenant?
faqs.answer: A Lieutenant is placed in Pay Level 10 with a scale of ₹ 56,100 to ₹ 1,77,500. On commissioning, pay is fixed at the first cell of Level 10, plus a Military Service Pay (MSP) of ₹ 15,500/- per month, Dearness Allowance (DA), and other applicable allowances. The estimated CTC is approx 17-18 Lakhs per annum.

faqs.question: What is the fixed stipend provided during the cadet training period?
faqs.answer: Gentlemen and Lady Cadets receive a fixed stipend of ₹ 56,100/- per month during the entire duration of their training at OTA Chennai.

faqs.question: What is the cost-of-training refund policy if a candidate withdraws?
faqs.answer: The entire cost of training is borne by the state. However, if an Officer Cadet is withdrawn or resigns for personal reasons (reasons other than medical or those beyond control), they are liable to refund the cost of training calculated at ₹ 20,482/- per week (as of 2026).

faqs.question: What are the promotion criteria for commissioned officers?
faqs.answer: Promotion is based on reckonable commissioned service: Lieutenant on commissioning; Captain after 2 years; Major after 6 years; Lt Colonel after 13 years; Colonel (TS) after 26 years; Colonel, Brigadier, and Major General are promotion ranks on selection basis subject to requisite service conditions.

faqs.question: What are the selection centers for the SSB interview?
faqs.answer: The SSB interviews will be conducted at selection centers in Prayagraj (Uttar Pradesh), Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh), Bengaluru (Karnataka), and Jalandhar (Punjab).

faqs.question: How many stages are there in the SSB interview selection?
faqs.answer: The SSB selection is a two-stage process. Stage-I is a screening test conducted on Day 1. Candidates who clear Stage-I proceed to Stage-II (Days 2 to 5), while those who fail are sent back on the first day.

faqs.question: Is travelling allowance provided for attending the SSB interview?
faqs.answer: Candidates appearing for the SSB interview for the first time for this type of commission are entitled to AC 3-Tier rail fare or bus fare within Indian geographical limits. No allowance is paid for subsequent attempts.

faqs.question: What insurance coverage is provided to cadets during training?
faqs.answer: Under the Army Group Insurance Fund (AGIF), cadets are insured for ₹ 1.25 Crore. A monthly subscription of ₹ 12,500/- is paid in advance by cadets. In case of 100% disability (invalidated out), ₹ 25 Lakhs is provided, and ₹ 5 Lakhs for 20% disability.

faqs.question: Are there restrictions on marriage for candidates?
faqs.answer: Yes. Candidates must not be married during training, nor are they allowed to live with parents/guardians. Anyone who marries after applying or during training will be withdrawn and required to refund all expenditures.

faqs.question: Can I use a DigiLocker certificate in place of original certificates at the SSB?
faqs.answer: No. DigiLocker certificates are strictly not accepted in lieu of original certificates. Physical original certificates must be produced.

faqs.question: What happens if I fail to report within 7 days of the specified date?
faqs.answer: Candidates who fail to report within 07 days of the reporting date will have their candidature cancelled, and the next candidate in the merit list will be considered.

faqs.question: Which language version of the notification is final in case of dispute?
faqs.answer: In case of any discrepancy or conflict between the English and Hindi versions of the notification, the English version shall prevail.

overview: Western Coalfields Limited (WCL), a premier Category-I Miniratna Public Sector Undertaking (PSU) under the Ministry of Coal, Government of India, and a key subsidiary of Coal India Limited, has announced the detailed recruitment notification for regular appointment to statutory supervisor positions. Headquartered at Nagpur, WCL operates highly mechanized opencast and underground coal mines across Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh through its 10 operational Areas.

The recruitment offers a total of 444 vacancies, divided into two key statutory profiles: 220 posts for Mining Sirdar in Technical & Supervisory (T&S) Grade-C, and 224 posts for Assistant Foreman (Trainee) (Electrical)/Electrical Supervisor in Technical & Supervisory (T&S) Grade-C. These statutory roles are crucial for the technical supervision, safety, and operations of WCL's highly mechanized coal mining projects.

Selection of candidates will be based purely on the marks obtained in the Computer Based Test (CBT). The online application window is open from July 20, 2026 at 10:00 AM and will close on August 10, 2026 at 11:55 PM. All eligible Indian nationals are encouraged to read the detailed eligibility requirements, educational qualifications, age limits, and instructions before applying online.

overview: Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), a statutory body under the administrative control of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, has released an official notification for the recruitment of Teaching Faculty positions on the post of Professors in ESIC PGIMSRs (Post Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences and Research) and ESIC Medical Colleges on a direct recruitment basis.

This recruitment campaign aims to fill a total of 118 regular Professor vacancies across 22 medical specialties including Anatomy, Anesthesiology, Biochemistry, Community Medicine, Emergency Medicine, General Medicine, General Surgery, Pathology, Pediatrics, and more. Selected candidates will be appointed to prestigious academic positions offering excellent career prospects and the opportunity to help build a premier social security healthcare and academic system in India.

Applications are invited from eligible Indian nationals (and other eligible categories of citizens specified in the instructions) through offline mode only. The completed application in the prescribed format, accompanied by self-attested documents and the application fee (where applicable), must reach the Regional Office in Delhi by 27 July 2026 (or 03 August 2026 for candidates residing in designated remote regions).

education: Essential for Medical Candidates:

1. A recognized medical qualification included in the First or Second Schedule or Part-II of the Third Schedule to the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956. (Holders of educational qualifications included in Part-II of the Third Schedule must also fulfill the conditions stipulated in section 13(3) of the said Act).
2. A post-graduate qualification e.g., MD (Doctor of Medicine) or MS (Master of Surgery) or a recognized qualification equivalent thereto in the respective subject or allied discipline.
Essential for Non-Medical Candidates:
1. A post-graduate qualification i.e., Master's Degree in the concerned subject or allied discipline.
2. A Doctorate degree from a recognized University in the respective subject or allied discipline.

Note: The respective subject or allied discipline should be as in the Table - I of Schedule I of the Medical Council of India - "Minimum Qualifications for Teachers in Medical Institutions Regulations, 1998".
Teaching Experience Requirements:
a) Four years teaching experience as a Reader or Associate Professor in a recognized medical college in the concerned specialty. OR

b) Three years teaching experience as Associate Professor in the concerned specialty in a recognized medical college with minimum of four research publications in indexed or national journals. These research publications must be published or accepted for publication in the Journals by the National Associations or Societies of the respective specialties as the First Author, on a cumulative basis with a minimum of two research publications published during the tenure of the Associate Professor.
Note: Teaching experience in any other post like General Duty Medical Officer (GDMO) shall NOT be considered for eligibility.

howToApply: Step 1: Obtain the official Application Form Performa appended at the end of the recruitment notification PDF from www.esic.gov.in.
Step 2: Fill out the application form completely in block letters, entering your specialty, Demand Draft details, personal details, contact details, permanent address, and qualifications.
Step 3: Paste a copy of your recent self-attested passport-size photograph firmly on the application form. Do NOT staple it.

Step 4: Procure a Demand Draft/Banker's Cheque of Rs. 500/- in favor of "ESI Fund Account No.2", drawn on any Scheduled Bank payable at Delhi (applicable only for General, OBC, EWS, and Departmental male candidates). Write your name and address on the reverse of the DD.

Step 7: Place everything in an envelope and super-scribe the envelope with "Application for the post of Professor for Medical Institutions" in bold letters.

faqs.question: What is the full form of ESIC?
faqs.answer: ESIC stands for Employees' State Insurance Corporation.

faqs.answer: ESIC functions under the Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India.

faqs.question: What is the nature of recruitment for the Professor positions?
faqs.answer: The positions are to be filled on a Direct Recruitment basis.

faqs.question: How many total Professor vacancies are announced?

faqs.question: Are there vacancies reserved for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD)?

faqs.answer: The age limit is "not exceeding 50 years" as of the closing date of application.

faqs.question: Is there any age relaxation for SC/ST and OBC candidates?
faqs.answer: Yes, the upper age limit is relaxed by up to 5 years for SC/ST candidates and up to 3 years for OBC candidates.

faqs.question: What is the age relaxation for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD)?
faqs.answer: PwBD candidates get an age relaxation of 10 years (subject to a maximum age limit of 56 years on the closing date).

faqs.answer: The crucial date is the general closing date for receipt of applications in India, which is 27 July 2026.

faqs.question: What are the essential qualifications for medical candidates?
faqs.answer: Medical candidates must have a recognized medical qualification (e.g., MBBS) included in the Schedules to the IMC Act 1956, and a post-graduate qualification (e.g., MD/MS) in the respective subject or allied discipline.

faqs.question: What are the qualifications for non-medical candidates?
faqs.answer: Non-medical candidates must possess a postgraduate Master's Degree and a Doctorate degree from a recognized University in the concerned subject or allied discipline.

faqs.question: How much teaching experience is required for the Professor post?
faqs.answer: Candidates must have either (a) 4 years of teaching experience as a Reader or Associate Professor, or (b) 3 years of teaching experience as an Associate Professor with a minimum of 4 research publications as first author on a cumulative basis.

faqs.question: Does GDMO experience count as teaching experience?
faqs.answer: No, teaching experience in any other post like General Duty Medical Officer (GDMO) shall not be considered for eligibility.

faqs.question: What is the application fee and how should it be paid?
faqs.answer: The fee is Rs. 500/- for General, OBC, EWS and Departmental male candidates, payable via a Demand Draft or Banker's Cheque in favor of "ESI Fund Account No.2", payable at Delhi. SC, ST, PwBD, Women, and Ex-Servicemen are exempted.

faqs.question: What is the selection process for the ESIC Professor post?
faqs.answer: Selection is done strictly through a Personal Interview. If the number of applicants is large, candidates may be shortlisted based on experience.

faqs.question: What are the qualifying marks in the personal interview?
faqs.answer: Out of 100 interview marks, the qualifying levels are: UR/EWS: 50 marks, OBC: 45 marks, and SC/ST/PwBD: 40 marks.

faqs.question: Can a candidate submit multiple applications under different categories?
faqs.answer: No. Submitting more than one application under different categories will make all of his/her applications liable to be rejected.

faqs.question: Are selected candidates liable to be posted anywhere in India?
faqs.answer: Yes, selected candidates are liable to be posted anywhere in India and must fill at least 10 state preference options in their application form.

faqs.answer: IHMCL stands for Indian Highways Management Company Limited. It is an initiative of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) jointly promoted along with its Concessionaires and Financial Institutions.

faqs.question: What is the primary role of IHMCL?
faqs.answer: IHMCL was established to implement and manage an efficient Electronic Toll Collection (ETC) system (FASTag) across national highways and deploy Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) to enhance highway management and improve traffic conditions.

faqs.question: What is the name and grade of the post advertised in this recruitment?
faqs.answer: The post is "Systems Engineer (ITS)" in the E-2 IDA Grade.

faqs.question: Is IHMCL a government or non-government company?
faqs.answer: IHMCL is a non-government company that has adopted the IDA pay pattern.

faqs.question: How many total vacancies are announced for Systems Engineer (ITS)?
faqs.answer: There is a total of 30 vacancies.

faqs.question: What is the category-wise distribution of the 30 vacancies?
faqs.answer: The category-wise distribution is: Unreserved (UR): 14, OBC (NCL): 8, SC: 4, ST: 1, and EWS: 3.

faqs.question: Is there any reservation for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD)?
faqs.answer: Yes, 01 post is reserved horizontally for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) out of the total 30 posts.

faqs.question: What is the pay scale and approximate monthly salary for Systems Engineer (ITS) in IHMCL?
faqs.answer: The pay scale is E-2 Grade Rs. 50,000 - 1,60,000/- with IDA Pattern. The starting basic pay is Rs. 50,000/-, and the approximate gross monthly salary is Rs. 100,000/-, including Dearness Allowance, Cafeteria Allowance, and House Rent Allowance (HRA) in X Class Cities (excluding statutory deductions like EPF and Income Tax).

faqs.question: What are the essential educational qualifications required to apply?
faqs.answer: Candidates must possess a Bachelor's Degree in Engineering in Information Technology, Computer Science, Electronics and Communications, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, or a combination of any of these engineering branches from a recognized University / Institute.

faqs.question: What is the age limit for applying to this recruitment?
faqs.answer: The candidate's age must be not less than 21 years and not exceeding 30 years as of the last date of receipt of online applications.

faqs.question: What is the crucial date for determining age limits and eligibility?
faqs.answer: The crucial date for determining eligibility, qualifications, and age is the last date prescribed for the receipt of online applications, which is 02.08.2026.

faqs.question: What is the opening and closing date for submitting online applications?
faqs.answer: The online registration starts on 04.07.2026 (10:00 AM) and closes on 02.08.2026 (06:00 PM).

faqs.question: Can final-year engineering students apply for this recruitment?
faqs.answer: Yes, candidates in their final year of the engineering degree program who are yet to receive their final results may apply. However, they must submit proof of passing the qualifying examination (Degree or Provisional Certificate) by 31.08.2026. Failure to do so will result in cancellation of their candidature.

faqs.question: What is the selection process for Systems Engineer (ITS) in IHMCL?
faqs.answer: Selection is done based on the merit of the valid GATE score. IHMCL also reserves the right to invite candidates for interview/interaction based on category-wise cut-offs subsequently decided by the company.

faqs.question: Which GATE disciplines are eligible for IHMCL Systems Engineer recruitment?
faqs.answer: A valid GATE score in Computer Science and Information Technology (CS), Electronics and Communications Engineering (EC), or Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DA) discipline is required.

faqs.question: Is there any discrepancy regarding GATE 2025 and 2026 scores in the PDF?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Selection Process section (Page 4) specifies selection based on the Valid GATE Score of 2026, while the document upload section (Page 5) and sample scorecard (Annexure-I) refer to the GATE 2025 Scorecard. Candidates should check the portal during registration and upload their valid scorecard accordingly.

faqs.question: Is there any service bond for selected candidates in IHMCL?
faqs.answer: Yes. All selected candidates must execute a Service Bond for Rs. 3.00 Lakhs to serve IHMCL for a minimum period of 3 years from the date of joining. Resignation or termination for misconduct within this 3-year period will require depositing Rs. 3.0 Lakhs.

faqs.question: What is the application fee for IHMCL recruitment?
faqs.answer: There is no application fee mentioned in the official notification PDF. Therefore, it is listed as "Not Mentioned in Official Notification" on our portal.

faqs.question: Is there an All India service liability for the Systems Engineer post?
faqs.answer: Yes. The post carries an All India service liability, meaning selected candidates must be willing to serve anywhere in India.

faqs.question: How can candidates apply for this recruitment?
faqs.answer: Candidates can apply ONLINE only by visiting http://www.ihmcl.co.in. Go to Careers -> New Openings, select the relevant advertisement, click "Online application", fill in the details, upload documents, and submit.

faqs.question: What happens if a candidate submits multiple applications?
faqs.answer: In case of multiple applications, only the last application successfully submitted will be considered, and all previous submissions will be rejected.

faqs.question: What are the document upload specifications for the online application?
faqs.answer: Upload specifications are: Photo and Signature <= 1 MB (jpg/jpeg/png/gif); Class X certificate, Engineering degree certificate, GATE Scorecard, and Caste certificate <= 2 MB (pdf).

faqs.question: What are the age relaxation benefits for reserved categories?
faqs.answer: Age relaxations are: SC/ST: 5 years; OBC (NCL): 3 years; Central Govt. employees (3 years continuous service in same/allied cadre): 5 years; J&K domicile (1980-1989): 5 years; PwBD: 10 years (General), 13 years (OBC), 15 years (SC/ST); Ex-Servicemen: Military service period plus 3 years.

faqs.question: Where will the interviews be conducted?
faqs.answer: As per the official notification, the interview will be held at a suitable place(s) decided by IHMCL. Specific venue details will be communicated directly to shortlisted candidates.

overview: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) has released the official notification for Advertisement No. 08/2026, inviting Online Recruitment Applications (ORA) for direct recruitment by selection to 48 permanent specialist vacancies across several ministries and departments of the Government of India. The recruitment window opens on 11th July 2026 and eligible candidates can submit their online applications until 31st July 2026 (18:00 Hours).

The advertised positions span multiple highly specialized domains. Major roles include Assistant Soil Chemist in Soil and Land Use Survey of India (SLUSI), Prosecutor in the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Specialist Grade III Assistant Professors across multiple medical disciplines (including Clinical Hematology, Endocrinology, Neonatology, Nuclear Medicine, Pulmonary Medicine, Paediatric Cardiology, and Surgical Gastroenterology) within the Central Health Service, Deputy Assistant Director and CCCO Entomologists in the National Centre for Vector Borne Diseases Control (NCVBDC), Junior Scientific Officer (Toxicology) in the Central Forensic Science Laboratory (CFSL), and Superintendent (Legal) in the Legislative Department under the Ministry of Law and Justice.

All appointments are permanent and carry high-grade pay scales under the 7th CPC (ranging from Level-7 up to Level-11 plus NPA for CHS teaching posts). Candidates are advised to carefully read the essential eligibility conditions, experience requirements, and specific service rules detailed below before filling out the online application form on the UPSC ORA portal.

Prosecutor (SFIO): Graduate in any discipline plus Bachelor’s degree in law (LLB) from a recognized University/Institute with 1 year experience in handling litigation & Court matters / administration of Law in a Government Organization; OR 5-year Integrated Law degree with 2 years’ experience in handling litigation & Court matters / administration of Law in a Government Organization. Assistant Professor (Endocrinology): Recognized MBBS degree + Post-graduate degree (D.M. / DNB in Endocrinology; OR M.D. in Medicine / Paediatrics with 2 years’ special training in Endocrinology). Experience: 3 years’ teaching experience in the speciality/super-speciality in a recognized teaching institution after obtaining first PG degree.

Assistant Professor (Neonatology): Recognized MBBS degree + PG degree (D.M. / DNB in Neonatology; OR M.D. in Paediatrics with 2 years' special training in Neonatology). Experience: 3 years' teaching experience in the speciality/super-speciality in a recognized teaching institution after obtaining first PG degree.

Assistant Professor (Nuclear Medicine): Recognized MBBS degree + PG degree (M.D. / DNB in Nuclear Medicine; OR M.D. / DNB in Radio-Therapy with 2 years’ experience in Nuclear Medicine; OR M.D. / DNB in Medicine with Diploma in Radiation Medicine/Nuclear Medicine; OR M.D. / DNB in Radio-Diagnosis with 2 years’ experience in Nuclear Medicine; OR M.D. in Bio-Physics or equivalent with Diploma in Radiation Medicine/Nuclear Medicine). Experience: 3 years’ teaching experience in the speciality/super-speciality after obtaining PG degree.

Assistant Professor (Pulmonary Medicine): Recognized MBBS degree + PG degree (M.D. / DNB in Pulmonary Medicine; OR M.D. / DNB in Respiratory Medicine / General Medicine / Paediatrics with 2 years’ special training in Pulmonary Medicine). Experience: 3 years’ teaching experience in the speciality/super-speciality after obtaining PG degree.

Assistant Professor (Paediatric Cardiology): Recognized MBBS degree + PG degree (D.M. / DNB in Paediatric Cardiology; OR D.M. / DNB in Cardiology; OR M.D. in Paediatrics with 2 years’ special training in Cardiology). Experience: 3 years’ teaching experience in the speciality/super-speciality after obtaining PG degree.

Assistant Professor (Surgical Gastroenterology): Recognized MBBS degree + PG degree (M.Ch. / DNB in Surgical Gastroenterology; OR M.S. in General Surgery with 2 years’ special training in Surgical Gastroenterology). Experience: 3 years’ teaching experience in the speciality/super-speciality after obtaining PG degree.

Deputy Assistant Director (Entomology): Master's Degree in Zoology with Entomology OR Master's degree in Public Health Entomology from a recognized University or institute. Experience: 3 years experience in teaching and/or research and/or control in the field of Medical Entomology or Public Health Entomology or Vector Borne Diseases. Desirable: Training in advanced Medical Entomology/Vector Biology Control/Public Health Entomology/Vector Borne Diseases.

Entomologist (CCCO): Master's Degree in Zoology with Entomology as one of the papers OR Master's degree in Public Health Entomology from a Recognized University or Institute. Experience: 3 years’ experience in teaching and/or research and/or control in the field of Medical Entomology or Public Health Entomology or Vector Borne Diseases.

Junior Scientific Officer (Toxicology): Master's Degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Pharmacology, Pharmacy, Forensic Science, or Associateship Diploma of the Institution of Chemists (by exam), with Chemistry as one of the subjects during all three years of B.Sc. level from a recognized University. Experience: 3 years’ experience in research and analytical work in the field of Toxicology in any central/state organisation, recognised institute, university, or forensic science labs under Central/State Govt. Desirable: Experience of working in a forensic science laboratory.

Superintendent (Legal): Bachelor's Degree in Law (LLB) from a recognized University. Experience: 2 years' experience as an Officer of the State Judicial Service; OR 2 years' experience in the Legal Department of a State; OR Central Govt servant with 2 years' experience in legal affairs; OR 2 years' experience as an Advocate at the Bar.
