howToApply: Step 1: Universal Registration - Visit the official UPSC Online Application Portal at https://upsconline.nic.in/ora/ and create your account under Universal Registration.
Step 2: Generate URN - Upon successful profile registration, a unique and constant Universal Registration Number (URN) is generated.
Step 3: Complete Common Application Form - Fill in your general credentials carefully. Upload your recent photograph and capture your live photograph in real-time as per prompt.
Step 4: Upload Signature - Sign three times (one below the other) using black ink on a plain white paper. Clear and legible scan/photo must be uploaded.

Step 5: Fill Post-Specific Form - Select the post you are applying for (e.g. Assistant Soil Chemist, Prosecutor SFIO, Assistant Professor) and provide the requisite academic qualifications and chronological employment details.

Step 6: Upload PDF Certificates - Separately upload self-attested documents/certificates in PDF format (such as Matriculation Certificate for DOB, Degree/Provisional Certificates, Chronological Experience Certificates, Caste/Community Certificate, or PwBD Certificate).

Step 7: Application Fee Payment - Pay the non-refundable application fee of Rs. 25/- online (Net Banking/Debit/Credit Card/UPI) if you are a Male UR/OBC/EWS candidate. Female/SC/ST/PwBD candidates are exempted from payment.

Step 8: Final Submission & Printout - Submit the form. A dynamic post-specific Application Number will be generated. Take a print out of the submitted application form for your own record and for bringing it at the time of the interview (do not mail printouts to UPSC).
documentsRequired: Matriculation/10th Standard or equivalent certificate showing Date of Birth (or marksheet issued by Central/State Board).
Degree/Diploma Certificate as proof of essential educational qualifications (or provisional certificate along with marksheets of all academic years).
Chronological Experience Certificate(s) from the Head of the Organisation/Department in the prescribed proforma, indicating duration, pay scale, and nature of duties performed.
Equivalent Qualification Order/Letter (if claiming equivalent educational criteria, specifying authority, number, and date).
Caste/Community Certificate (SC/ST/OBC) in the prescribed format from a competent authority, indicating candidate’s caste, act, and residency details.
OBC Non-Creamy Layer Declaration in the prescribed format as on the crucial date.
Certificate of Disability (PwBD) in the prescribed proforma issued by a Medical Board duly constituted by Central or State Government.
Name Change Proof (Husband’s passport, marriage certificate, divorce deed, or gazette publication/deed poll with newspaper clippings) if candidate’s name changed after matriculation.
Regular Government Servant Declaration (if seeking age relaxation under Central/UT Govt servant category) on office letterhead.
importantInstructions: CRITICAL WARNING: Candidates must ensure that all details filled in the online application are true and correct. If any claim or document is found to be false/fabricated at any stage or during the interview, the candidate will be rejected and debarred permanently or for a specified period from UPSC exams and Central Government jobs.

EXPERIENCE CLARIFICATION: The period of experience rendered on a part-time basis, daily wages, or as a visiting or guest faculty will NOT be counted while calculating valid experience for shortlisting.

NO WITHDRAWAL OF APPLICATION: Candidates will not be permitted to withdraw their applications or request any correction, alteration, or modification in any field of the application form once it has been submitted.

CORRESPONDENCE EMAIL: All communications, including interview schedules, call letters, and additional certificate demands, will be made through EMAIL ONLY. Candidates must provide a correct, active, and regularly monitored email address.

NO NEED TO SEND PRINT OUTS: Candidates are strictly instructed NOT to submit any physical prints of online applications or supporting documents to the Commission by post or by hand. These must be produced only if called for an interview.

PRESCRIBED PROFORMA ONLY: Experience certificates, Caste certificates, and PwBD disability certificates must strictly follow the prescribed proformas available on the UPSC official website (https://upsc.gov.in/recruitment/recruitment-performas).

TRAVELING ALLOWANCE: If required to attend a personal interview in Delhi, the Commission contributes to traveling expenses for outstation candidates at a rate corresponding to Second Class Mail railway fare by the shortest route, paid on the spot (or via bank transfer later if the interview is held outside Delhi).

faqs.question: What is the recruitment advertisement number and where can I apply?
faqs.answer: The recruitment is under Advertisement No. 08/2026. Eligible candidates must apply online through the official Online Recruitment Application (ORA) portal of the Union Public Service Commission at https://upsconline.nic.in/ora/.

faqs.question: What are the start and end dates for submitting the UPSC 08/2026 online application?
faqs.answer: The online application portal opens on 11th July 2026, and the closing date for submission is 18:00 Hours (6:00 PM) on 31st July 2026.

faqs.question: How many posts are advertised in UPSC Advertisement No. 08/2026?
faqs.answer: A total of 48 vacancies across 13 different specialist and teaching positions are advertised under Advertisement No. 08/2026.

faqs.question: Is the age limit relaxed for reserved categories in this recruitment?
faqs.answer: Yes. The normal upper age limit is relaxed by 5 years for SC/ST, 3 years for OBC, and up to 10 years for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) in respect of vacancies reserved for them.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the post of Assistant Soil Chemist?
faqs.answer: Candidates must possess a Master's Degree in Agriculture or Agricultural Chemistry with specialization in Soil Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, or Soil Science, plus 3 years' experience in Soil and Water analysis under Central/State Govt, UTs, autonomous/statutory bodies, PSU, or a recognized research/university institution.

faqs.question: What is the eligibility criteria for the Prosecutor post in the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO)?
faqs.answer: Must have a Graduate Degree in any discipline + Bachelor's Degree in Law (LLB) with 1 year's experience in litigation/court matters in a Government Organization; OR a 5-year Integrated LLB degree with 2 years' experience. LLM is desirable.

faqs.question: What is the pay scale for Specialist Grade III Assistant Professors?
faqs.answer: Teaching positions in the Central Health Service are under Level-11 of the 7th CPC Pay Matrix (Rs. 67,700 - 2,08,700) plus Non-Practicing Allowance (NPA) as per rules.

faqs.question: What are the qualifying marks for the UPSC personal interview?
faqs.answer: The total marks of the interview are 100. Category-wise minimum qualifying marks (suitability level) are: UR/EWS - 50 marks, OBC - 45 marks, and SC/ST/PwBD - 40 marks.

faqs.question: What is the application fee and who is exempted?
faqs.answer: The application fee is Rs. 25/- (Rupees Twenty Five Only) for Unreserved, OBC, and EWS male candidates. All Female candidates, SC, ST, and PwBD candidates are completely exempted from payment.

faqs.question: What are the educational qualifications for Deputy Assistant Director (Entomology)?
faqs.answer: Requires a Master's Degree in Zoology with Entomology or a Master's degree in Public Health Entomology from a recognized university or institute, plus 3 years of experience in teaching/research/control in Medical/Public Health Entomology.

faqs.question: Can I apply for multiple posts under this advertisement?
faqs.answer: Yes. Candidates can apply for more than one post if they meet the specific eligibility requirements. However, they must submit separate online applications and pay the separate fee for each post applied.

faqs.question: What is the required educational qualification for JSO (Toxicology)?
faqs.answer: Master's Degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Pharmacology, Pharmacy, or Forensic Science, with Chemistry as a subject during all three years of B.Sc. level.

faqs.question: Is part-time or daily-wage experience counted as valid experience?
faqs.answer: No. The notification clearly states that experience gained on a part-time basis, daily wages, or as a visiting or guest faculty will NOT be counted for shortlisting.

faqs.question: Where will the selected candidates be posted?
faqs.answer: Appointments have All India Service Liability (AISL). However, specific headquarters are New Delhi (SFIO, NCVBDC, Legislative Dept), Delhi (CHS), SLUSI Centres (Delhi, Noida, Kolkata, Nagpur, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Ranchi), and CFSL Centres.

faqs.question: Are there any restrictions on private practice for the Assistant Professor roles?
faqs.answer: Yes. Selected Assistant Professors belong to the Teaching Specialist Sub-cadre of the Central Health Service, and private practice of any kind whatsoever (including laboratory or consultation practice) is strictly prohibited.

faqs.question: What is the probation period for these positions?
faqs.answer: The probation period is 1 year for Specialist Grade III Assistant Professors, and 2 years for all other posts (such as Assistant Soil Chemist, Prosecutor SFIO, Entomologist, JSO Toxicology, and Superintendent Legal).

faqs.question: Is there a mandatory induction training during probation?
faqs.answer: Yes. For roles like Assistant Soil Chemist, Prosecutor SFIO, and Deputy Assistant Director (Entomology), successful completion of a mandatory induction training of at least two weeks is a prerequisite for probation clearance.

faqs.question: Do I need to send physical copies of my application or certificates to UPSC?
faqs.answer: No. Printouts of the online application or other documents must NOT be sent to the Commission by post or hand. Shortlisted candidates must bring them when called for interview.

faqs.question: How can I contact the UPSC helpdesk for application queries?
faqs.answer: You can contact the dedicated helpline at 011-24041001 or 011-40303444, or email upscsoap@nic.in. The helpline operates from 10:00 AM to 5:30 PM on all working days.

faqs.question: Will I be paid any traveling allowance for attending the interview?
faqs.answer: Yes. Outstation candidates summoned for interview are contributed Second Class Mail railway fare by the shortest route to Delhi and back (paid on the spot or via bank transfer on submitting TA claims).

faqs.question: Is the National Pension Scheme applicable to these roles?
faqs.answer: Yes, selected candidates will be governed by the New Pension Scheme (NPS) which became effective on 1st January 2004.

faqs.question: What are the skill requirements for uploading signature?
faqs.answer: Candidates must sign three times (one below the other) using black ink on a plain white paper and upload the clear PDF/Image during application submission.

The recruitment offers a total of 95 apprenticeships across multiple engineering, commercial practice, and trade streams. These positions are distributed across three prime ISTRAC facilities located in Bengaluru (Karnataka), Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh), and Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair, Andaman & Nicobar Islands).

overview: The Indian Army, Ministry of Defence, Government of India, has officially announced the commencement of the registration process for the 68th Short Service Commission (Technical) Women Course (April 2027) with Advertisement Number SSCW(T)-68. This is a premier officer entry scheme that offers a prestigious career opportunity to unmarried female engineering graduates and widows of defence personnel. The recruitment aims to select talented, technical-minded women to join as commissioned officers in the Indian Army and lead from the front.

A total of 30 vacancies have been notified, including 29 positions across various core engineering streams (Civil: 07, Computer Science: 04, Electrical: 03, Electronics: 06, Mechanical: 09) and 1 vacancy for Widows of Defence Personnel who died in harness. The course will commence in April 2027 at the prestigious Officers Training Academy (OTA), Gaya, Bihar. Online applications will be accepted through the official recruitment portal of the Indian Army starting from 08 July 2026 and will close on 06 August 2026.

To be eligible for the Indian Army SSCW Tech 68 Course, candidates must satisfy the nationality, age, educational qualification, and physical standards. Unmarried female engineering graduates who have completed or are in the final year of B.E. / B.Tech from recognized universities/institutions are eligible to apply. The age limit for SSC (Tech) entries is 20 to 27 years as on 01 April 2027. For widows of defence personnel, the maximum age limit is relaxed up to 35 years as on 01 April 2027. Essential physical standards include clear targets for running, push-ups, pull-ups, sit-ups, squats, and swimming, ensuring the candidates possess the physical fitness required for military training and leadership.

faqs.question: What is the entry name and course code of this Indian Army recruitment?
faqs.answer: The entry is Short Service Entry (Technical) under the 68th Short Service Commission (Technical) Women Course starting in April 2027, with Ad No. SSCW(T)-68.

faqs.question: When does the online application open and close?
faqs.answer: Online applications open on 08 July 2026 at 15:00 HRS and close on 06 August 2026 at 15:00 HRS.

faqs.question: What is the total number of vacancies advertised for SSCW(T)-68?
faqs.answer: A total of 30 vacancies are advertised (29 for core technical streams of the main entry and 1 for Widows of Defence Personnel).

faqs.question: What is the vacancy breakdown across different engineering streams?
faqs.answer: The technical vacancies are Civil Engineering: 07, Computer Science: 04, Electrical Engineering: 03, Electronics Engineering: 06, and Mechanical Engineering: 09.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for the main technical course?
faqs.answer: Unmarried female engineering graduates who have completed B.E./B.Tech or are in the final year of study in the notified branches are eligible.

faqs.question: What is the age limit for the main technical course?
faqs.answer: Candidates must be between 20 and 27 years of age as on 01 April 2027. That means candidates must be born between 01 April 2000 and 31 March 2007 (both days inclusive).

faqs.question: What is the eligibility and age limit for Widows of Defence Personnel?
faqs.answer: Widows of defence personnel who died in harness and have not remarried can apply up to a maximum age of 35 years as on 01 April 2027.

faqs.question: What are the two entries for Widows of Defence Personnel and their qualifications?
faqs.answer: They can apply for: (1) SSCW (Non-Tech)(Non-UPSC): requires Graduation in any stream. (2) SSCW (Tech): requires B.E./B.Tech in any engineering stream.

faqs.question: Where is the training academy located for SSCW(T)-68?
faqs.answer: The pre-commission training will be conducted at the prestigious Officers Training Academy (OTA), Gaya, Bihar.

faqs.question: What is the duration of the training course at OTA Gaya?
faqs.answer: The pre-commission training duration is 49 weeks (excluding term breaks).

faqs.question: Is there any application fee for applying to this post?
faqs.answer: Not Mentioned in Official Notification. No fee is specified; candidates can register and apply online absolutely free.

faqs.question: What is the stipend paid to candidates during the training period?
faqs.answer: During training, candidates are paid a fixed stipend of Rs. 56,100/- per month (starting pay in Level 10).

faqs.question: What rank is awarded upon successful completion of the training?
faqs.answer: On successful commissioning, candidates are granted the rank of Lieutenant in the Indian Army.

faqs.question: What is the starting basic pay of a Lieutenant on commissioning?
faqs.answer: The basic pay of a Lieutenant is Rs. 56,100/- to Rs. 1,77,500/- under Level 10 of the Pay Matrix, plus Rs. 15,500/- per month Military Service Pay (MSP).

faqs.question: What is the minimum physical fitness standard required for selection?
faqs.answer: The minimum physical standards are 2.4 Km run in 13 minutes, 15 push-ups, 2 pull-ups, 25 sit-ups, 2 sets of 30 squats, 2 sets of 10 lunges, and basic swimming knowledge.

faqs.question: Are final year appearing candidates eligible to apply?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided they are in their final year/semester and will complete their course and produce passing proof with marksheets of all semesters by 01 April 2027.

faqs.question: Is there any negative marking in the screening or SSB?
faqs.answer: No. The selection is based on academic merit screening and a 5-day Services Selection Board (SSB) personal interview.

faqs.question: What are the centers for the SSB interview?
faqs.answer: The SSB interview centers are Prayagraj (Uttar Pradesh), Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh), Bengaluru (Karnataka), and Jalandhar (Punjab).

faqs.question: How is the final merit list prepared?
faqs.answer: The final merit list is prepared stream-wise based on the marks obtained by candidates in the SSB interview only, subject to medical fitness.

faqs.question: Are candidates eligible for Travelling Allowance (TA) for attending the SSB?
faqs.answer: Yes. First-time candidates appearing for a particular type of commission are entitled to AC-3 Tier rail fare or bus fare within Indian limits.

faqs.question: Can I request a change of my SSB interview date or center?
faqs.answer: No. Request for change of SSB interview date or selection center will NOT be entertained under any circumstances.

faqs.question: Does completing this course guarantee a Permanent Commission in the Indian Army?
faqs.answer: No. Candidates are granted a Short Service Commission for a tenure of 10 years (extendable to 14 years). Option for Permanent Commission can be exercised in the 10th year of service.

faqs.question: Can married female engineering graduates apply?
faqs.answer: No. The recruitment is strictly open to unmarried female candidates, except for widows of defence personnel who have not remarried.

faqs.question: Where should Widows of Defence Personnel send their offline applications?
faqs.answer: They must send their application directly to: Directorate General of Recruiting, Rtg A (TGC) Section, West Block-III, R K Puram, New Delhi - 110066 on or before 21 August 2026.

faqs.question: Are e-certificates downloaded from DigiLocker accepted as originals at the SSB center?

syllabus.section: Section A: Technical Knowledge for Mining Sirdar
topics: Coal Mines Regulations, 2017: Provisions, chapters, definitions, duties of Mining Sirdar, Overman, Shot-firer, Assistant Manager, and Manager.
Mine Safety & Health: Provisions of Mines Act 1952, Mines Rules 1955, and safety guidelines issued by DGMS. Personal protective equipment, first-aid, health hazards.

Mine Gases & Ventilation: Properties of fire damp, carbon monoxide, black damp, white damp, nitrous fumes. Detection using flame safety lamps, gas detectors, and multisensor monitors. General principles of underground ventilation, distribution of air, ventilation structures (doors, regulators, stoppings, air-crossings), auxiliary fans.

Roof Support & Strata Control: Roof behavior, roof testing methods, types of support (timber, steel prop, chocks, roof bolts, cable bolts), Systematic Support Rules (SSR) under CMR 2017, support setting and withdrawal precautions.

Explosives & Blasting: Permitted explosives, liquid oxygen explosives, detonators, shot-firing tools, shot-firing procedures in opencast and underground mines, precautions against misfires, blown-out shots, toxic fumes, and safety during blasting.
Opencast Mining Operations: Bench parameters (height, width, slope), dump parameters, transport roads, machinery safety (dumpers, shovels, draglines, surface miners).

Mine Fires & Inundation: Spontaneous combustion, causes of mine fires, prevention, fire-fighting, sealing-off areas, self-rescuers, safety precautions against water inundation, barrier pillars, water dams, safety during heavy rains.

syllabus.section: Section A: Technical Knowledge for Surveyor (Mining)
topics: General Surveying Principles: Chain surveying, compass surveying, plane table surveying, leveling, contouring, theodolite surveying, tacheometry, trigonometric leveling, astronomical observation.
Advanced Surveying Instruments: Electronic Distance Measurement (EDM), Total Station, GPS/GNSS surveying, 3D laser scanners, LIDAR, drone surveying applications in open-cast mines.
Mine Plans & Sections: statutory requirements for preparation and maintenance of mine plans, scales, symbols, colors, accuracy limits as per CMR 2017. Correlation of surface and underground surveys.
Geodetic Surveying & Triangulation: Principles of triangulation, trilateration, adjustment of triangulation networks, error calculations, least squares adjustments.
Underground Surveying: Setting out underground curves, gradient lines, drift alignments, connection of workings, borehole surveying, dialing and leveling in underground mines.
Subsidence Surveying: Principles, measurement of ground movement, monitoring techniques, calculation of tilt, strain, curvature, subsidence control.

syllabus.section: Section B: General Awareness & Mental Ability (Common to Both Posts)
topics: General Knowledge & Awareness: Indian History, Indian Geography, Constitution of India, Civics, General Science, Sports, National & International Current Affairs, environmental science.

Reasoning & Mental Ability: Analogies, similarities and differences, spatial visualization, spatial orientation, relationship concepts, arithmetical reasoning, verbal and figure classification, number series, coding-decoding.
Quantitative Aptitude: Number systems, decimals, fractions, percentage, ratio and proportion, average, interest (simple and compound), profit and loss, discount, time and work, time and distance.

faqs.question: What is the crucial date for determining age and qualification eligibility in this NCL recruitment?
faqs.answer: The crucial date is 05-08-2026. All academic qualifications, DGMS competency certificates, and caste/category credentials must be held on or before this date.

faqs.question: What are the two statutory posts advertised and how many vacancies are there?
faqs.answer: The recruitment is for: (1) Mining Sirdar T&S Gr. C (254 posts) and (2) Surveyor (Mining) T&S Gr. B (5 posts). The total vacancies across both posts is 259.

faqs.question: Are candidates with a B.E./B.Tech in Mining Engineering eligible to apply for the Mining Sirdar post?
faqs.answer: Yes. Candidates with a Degree in Mining Engineering or a 3-year Diploma in Mining Engineering are fully eligible, provided they also possess a valid Overman Certificate of Competency (or Mining Sirdar Certificate), Gas Testing Certificate, and First Aid Certificate.

faqs.question: Is a Gas Testing Certificate and First Aid Certificate mandatory for both positions?
faqs.answer: No. Gas Testing and First Aid certificates are strictly mandatory for the Mining Sirdar post. For the Surveyor (Mining) post, they are NOT mandatory; only a Matriculation/Diploma and a valid Surveyor Certificate of Competency issued by DGMS are required.

faqs.question: What is the application fee for different categories of candidates?
faqs.answer: Candidates belonging to UR, OBC (NCL), and EWS must pay a total fee of Rs. 1,180/- (Rs. 1000 application fee + Rs. 180 GST). Candidates belonging to SC, ST, PwBD, ESM, and Departmental candidates are completely exempt from paying any fees.

faqs.question: Is there any negative marking in the NCL Computer Based Test (CBT)?
faqs.answer: No. There is no negative marking in the CBT. Candidates are awarded 1 mark for each correct answer, and no marks are deducted for incorrect or unattempted questions.

faqs.question: What is the exam pattern and distribution of marks for the CBT?
faqs.answer: The exam consists of 100 multiple-choice questions for 100 marks to be solved in 90 minutes. It has two sections: Section A contains 70 questions on post-specific technical/subject knowledge, and Section B contains 30 questions on general awareness, aptitude, and reasoning.

faqs.question: What are the minimum qualifying marks required in the CBT to be considered for selection?
faqs.answer: The minimum qualifying marks are 50% (50 out of 100 marks) for Unreserved (UR) and EWS candidates, and 40% (40 out of 100 marks) for SC, ST, OBC (NCL), PwBD, and ESM candidates.

faqs.question: What is the salary scale for Mining Sirdar and Surveyor posts?
faqs.answer: Mining Sirdar is a T&S Grade C post with a starting basic pay of Rs. 31,852.56 per month. Surveyor (Mining) is a T&S Grade B post with a starting basic pay of Rs. 34,391.65 per month. This basic pay is supplemented by allowances like DA, HRA, bonuses, medical facilities, etc.

faqs.question: Is there an interview process after qualifying the CBT exam?
faqs.answer: No. As per Central Government guidelines, there is no personal interview for Group B and Group C non-executive posts. Selection is based purely on the CBT merit score, followed by Document Verification and Medical Fitness.

faqs.question: Where will the Computer Based Test (CBT) be conducted?
faqs.answer: The CBT will be conducted in various cities of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, including Singrauli, Bhopal, Jabalpur, Gwalior, Indore, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Lucknow, Sonebhadra, and Noida.

faqs.question: Can candidates residing in states other than MP and UP apply for these jobs?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is a national-level recruitment. Any Indian citizen meeting the eligibility criteria can apply, regardless of their state of residence.

faqs.question: How is the final merit list prepared in case of a tie in CBT marks?
faqs.answer: In case of a tie in CBT marks, the tie is resolved by placing the candidate older in age higher in merit. If the tie still persists, the candidate with higher marks in their professional qualification (Degree/Diploma) is preferred.

faqs.question: Do I need to send physical copies of my application or certificates to NCL?
faqs.answer: No. Under no circumstances should you send a printout of the application or physical certificates to NCL. The entire application and document submission process is online.

faqs.question: Are final-year students eligible to apply?
faqs.answer: No. Candidates whose final results have not been declared, or who have not received their DGMS competency certificates on or before the crucial date of 05-08-2026, are NOT eligible to apply.

overview: IIFCL Projects Limited (IPL), a prestigious wholly-owned subsidiary of India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (IIFCL) - a 100% Government of India Enterprise, has officially announced a rolling advertisement for the engagement of Individual Consultants (IC) on a full-time, contractual basis. With a mandate to deliver expert Financial & Infrastructure Advisory services to Central & State Governments, Local Bodies, and Private Developers across India, IPL is building a robust database of highly qualified professionals. This rolling recruitment campaign operates continuously throughout the year, allowing eligible candidates to submit their applications at any time to be considered for active project requirements in multiple sectors, including roads, highways, ports, power, water supply, renewable energy, tourism, and solid waste management.

This recruitment campaign offers a wide array of opportunities, spanning across 65 specialized consultant profiles. These encompass diverse areas such as Project & Contract Management, Procurement, Financial & Costing, IT & MIS, Digital Public Infrastructure, Legal Management, Corporate Communications, Tourism Development, Master Planning, PPP & Investment, and Environmental Affairs. The vacancies are not fixed to a static count, as hiring is on a rolling basis, meaning candidate requirements are fulfilled dynamically as mandates arise. The position grades range from Young Professionals to Senior Consultants (Grades I, II, and III) based on years of post-qualification experience. Selected professionals will be stationed at IPL's Head Office in New Delhi or branch offices and project sites across various States including Amaravati (AP), Chennai, Ahmedabad, the Northeast Region, and other locations on an "Anywhere in India" basis.

The eligibility criteria vary depending on the specific IC Code of interest. Educational requirements range from Graduate degrees in Engineering (B.E./B.Tech), Architecture, Planning, or Law (LLB/LLM) to Postgraduate degrees, MBA/PGDM, CA, CWA, or CFA from recognized premium national or international institutes. Remuneration is highly attractive and structured based on experience: Young Professionals receive a fixed pay of ₹70,000 per month; Grade I Consultants receive between ₹80,000 and ₹1,45,000; Grade II Consultants earn from ₹1,45,000 to ₹2,65,000; and Senior Consultants (Grade III) are eligible for ₹2,65,000 to ₹3,30,000 per month. The upper age limits are 32, 45, 50, and 62 years respectively.

Interested and qualified candidates can apply either by email or physical post. The application window is open for exactly one year from the date of publishing the advertisement, running on a rolling basis. Candidate selection is based entirely on an Interview process (either in Delhi or via online mode), which follows preliminary shortlisting of applicants matching the company's rigorous experience, suitability, and business criteria. There is no application fee for any category, making this a transparent, merit-based entry into one of India's leading government-backed infrastructure advisory firms.

faqs.question: What is the full form of IPL, and who is its parent organization?
faqs.answer: IPL stands for IIFCL Projects Limited, which is a wholly-owned subsidiary of India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (IIFCL), a 100% Government of India Enterprise.

faqs.question: What is the main objective of IIFCL Projects Limited (IPL)?
faqs.answer: The main objective of IPL is to provide Financial & Infrastructure Advisory services to various Central & State Governments, their affiliates, Local Bodies, and Private Developers, along with Capacity Building and Policy Advocacy services.

faqs.question: What is the nature of the engagement for the Individual Consultants (IC) positions?
faqs.answer: The engagement of Individual Consultants is on a full-time, contractual basis. Selected candidates are not allowed to take up any other appointment, engagement, or assignment during their contract period.

faqs.question: Where will the selected Individual Consultants be stationed?
faqs.answer: Selected consultants are expected to be stationed at IPL's Head Office in Delhi, and/or any of its branch offices, and/or across various States wherein IPL is currently working or intends to work under mandate.

faqs.question: What does rolling recruitment mean for this IPL notification?
faqs.answer: It means that applications are accepted and evaluated throughout the year on an as-and-when needed basis. IPL maintains an active database of applications, and candidates are selected from this pool whenever vacancies arise in specific areas of work.

faqs.question: What is the duration of the rolling applications window?
faqs.answer: The applications window is open for exactly one year from the date of publishing the advertisement.

faqs.question: What are the four grades of Individual Consultants, and what is their required experience?
faqs.answer: The grades are: (1) Young Professional with 1 year experience; (2) Consultant Grade I with 3 - 8 years experience; (3) Consultant Grade II with 8 - 15 years experience; and (4) Senior Consultant with 15 years or more experience.

faqs.question: What is the monthly remuneration for a Young Professional?
faqs.answer: A Young Professional is paid a fixed monthly consolidated remuneration of ₹70,000.

faqs.question: What is the monthly salary range for a Consultant Grade I?
faqs.answer: The monthly remuneration range for Consultant Grade I is ₹80,000 to ₹1,45,000.

faqs.question: What is the monthly salary range for a Consultant Grade II?
faqs.answer: The monthly remuneration range for Consultant Grade II is ₹1,45,000 to ₹2,65,000.

faqs.question: What is the monthly salary range for a Senior Consultant (Grade III)?
faqs.answer: The monthly remuneration range for Senior Consultant (Grade III) is ₹2,65,000 to ₹3,30,000.

faqs.question: How is the final remuneration decided for selected candidates?
faqs.answer: The final remuneration within the corresponding grade band is decided based on the candidate's expectations, experience, and expertise. The decision of IPL is final and binding.

faqs.question: Is TA/DA provided for official tours during the engagement?
faqs.answer: Yes. Consultants are allowed to undertake official tours as required by their duties, and TA/DA and Hotel Accommodation are paid or reimbursed as per the company's policy.

faqs.question: What are the upper age limits for different grades of consultants?
faqs.answer: The upper age limits are: 32 years for Young Professional, 45 years for Consultant Grade I, 50 years for Consultant Grade II, and 62 years for Senior Consultant.

faqs.question: What are the essential academic qualifications required to apply?
faqs.answer: Qualifications depend on the specific IC Code but generally include regular Graduation/Post Graduation in Engineering (B.E./B.Tech/B.Arch/B.Plan/M.Tech/M.Plan), Master's/Postgraduate degrees, MBA, CA, CWA, CFA, LLB, or LLM from recognized premier institutes.

faqs.question: Are candidates with degrees from foreign universities eligible?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided they can produce an equivalency certificate issued by a Competent Authority certifying that their foreign qualification is treated at par with qualifications offered by Indian Institutes/Universities.

faqs.question: What is the selection procedure for these consultant posts?
faqs.answer: The selection is done through a Personal Interview after preliminary screening and shortlisting of applications based on qualifications, experience, suitability, city preference, and business requirements.

faqs.question: Where will the Personal Interviews be conducted, and is travel allowance provided?
faqs.answer: Shortlisted applicants will attend the interview in Delhi or online. No travel expense reimbursement (TA/DA) is paid for appearing in the interview.

faqs.question: What is the initial period of engagement for these contractual positions?
faqs.answer: Individual Consultants are engaged for an initial fixed period of two years.

faqs.question: Can the period of contract be extended, and what is the maximum limit?
faqs.answer: Yes, the contract can be extended by one year at a time up to a maximum tenure of 5 years (i.e. 2+1+1+1 years), contingent on a satisfactory Annual Performance Review based on KPIs.

faqs.question: How can candidates apply for this recruitment, and are there different email addresses?
faqs.answer: Candidates must apply by email or post. There are separate email addresses: recruitment1@iifclprojects.com for IC Codes 01 to 10; recruitment2@iifclprojects.com for IC Codes 13 to 46; and recruitment3@iifclprojects.com for IC Codes 11, 12, and 47 to 65.

iaf-agniveervayu-musician-2026.title: Recruitment of Agniveervayu (Musician) - Intake 01/2027
overview: The Indian Air Force (IAF) has released an official recruitment notification inviting unmarried Indian male and female candidates from all districts of all States and Union Territories of India to appear in a pre-registered recruitment rally to join as Agniveervayu (Musician) under Intake 01/2027. This prestigious opportunity is specifically aimed at recruiting talented musicians to play different musical instruments as part of the Air Force Band. The online registration commences on July 20, 2026 at 11:00 AM and will conclude on August 2, 2026 at 11:00 PM. Only registered candidates who are issued a Provisional Admit Card will be allowed to participate in the pre-registered recruitment rally.

The recruitment rally will be held from August 31, 2026 to September 9, 2026 at two designated Selection Centers: 2 ASC C/O Race Course Camp, Air Force Station New Delhi, and 7 ASC, No. 1 Cubbon Road, Bengaluru (Karnataka). Candidates must indicate their preference order of these two venues during online registration. The enrolment is for a strict tenure of four years under the Agnipath scheme, offering customized monthly pay packages starting from ₹30,000/- in the 1st year to ₹40,000/- in the 4th year, with a one-time exit "Seva Nidhi" package of approximately ₹10.04 Lakhs (excluding interest) on completion of service. Up to 25% of each batch will be enrolled in the regular cadre of the Indian Air Force as Airmen based on organizational requirements and performance.

The selection methodology is highly structured, including initial verification of eligibility, a Physical Fitness Test (PFT-I & II), a written test in English, a Music Proficiency Test (MPT) in playing musical instruments, and a comprehensive Medical Examination. The educational requirement is 10th / Matriculation or equivalent with minimum pass marks, along with specified proficiency and certification in playing musical instruments. Only candidates born between 01 January 2005 and 01 July 2009 (both dates inclusive) are eligible to apply. No physical or offline forms are entertained, and candidates must pay a registration fee of ₹100/- plus 18% GST online through Net Banking, Debit Cards, Credit Cards, or UPI.

education: Educational Qualification: Passed Matriculation / 10th or equivalent with minimum pass marks from any Central, State, and UT Government recognized School / Board as on the date of registration.

Instrument Tuning: Candidates must be able to tune individual instruments (for instruments requiring tuning) and match unknown notes on vocal or instruments.

Instrument Proficiency (List A or B): Must have proficiency in playing at least one instrument from the following standard lists:

• List A (Wind / Brass / Strings): Concert Flute / Piccolo, Oboe, Clarinet in Eb / Bb, Saxophone in Eb / Bb, French Horn in F / Bb, Trumpet in Eb / C / Bb, Trombone in Bb / G, Baritone, Euphonium, Bass / Tuba in Eb / Bb.

• List B (Keyboard / Percussion / Others): Keyboard / Organ / Piano, Guitar (Acoustic / Lead / Bass), Violin, Viola, String Bass, Percussion / Drums (Acoustic / Electronic), All Indian Classical Instruments.
Desirable: Proficiency in playing two instruments (one each from List A and List B above) is highly desirable.
Musical Experience Certification (Must possess any one of the following):

1. Grade 5th or equivalent or above in one instrument from a recognized music institute such as Trinity College London (TCL), Royal Schools of Music (RSM), KM Music Conservatory, Bangalore School of Music, TSM, GMI, Berklee School of Music, etc.
2. OR Diploma or equivalent in the field of music for candidates performing Hindustani or Carnatic Classical Music from any recognized university.

3. OR Certificate of participation / awards presented at various events. For such candidates, performance or playing of blowing instruments with staff notation as mentioned in educational qualifications is required.

medicalStandards:
Height Standards:
• Male Candidates: Minimum acceptable height is 162 cms.
• Female Candidates: Minimum acceptable height is 152 cms.
• Height Relaxation: For candidates of North East or hilly regions of Uttarakhand ethnicity, a lower minimum height of 147 cms is accepted. For candidates of Lakshadweep ethnicity, the minimum height is 150 cms.
Weight Standards: Proportionate to height and age as applicable for the Indian Air Force.

Chest Standards:
• Male Candidates: Well proportioned and well-developed chest wall. Minimum chest circumference should be 77 cms and the chest expansion must be at least 05 cms.
• Female Candidates: Well proportioned chest wall with a minimum range of chest expansion of 05 cms.
Hearing: Normal hearing (able to hear a forced whisper from a distance of 6 meters by each ear separately).
Dental Standards: Healthy gums, good set of teeth, and a minimum of 14 dental points. Candidates wearing fixed or removable orthodontic appliances will be declared unfit.

Visual Standards:
• Visual Acuity: 6/12 each eye, correctable to 6/6 each eye.
• Refractive Error limits: Hypermetropia: +2.0D, Myopia: -1D (including ± 0.50 D Astigmatism).
• Colour Vision: CP-II.
• Spectacles / LASIK: Candidates using spectacles must bring a latest prescription (not older than 1 month) bearing diopter measurement, name, signature, stamp, and registration number of the Ophthalmologist. Candidates with a history of LASIK / PRK will NOT be accepted.
Gynaecological Examination (for females): The clinical examination covers external genitalia, hernia orifices, perineum, and any clinical evidence of stress urinary incontinence or genital prolapse.

Gender & Pregnancy: Candidates with predominant characteristics of the opposite gender or who have undergone gender reassignment surgery will be rejected. Any female candidate found pregnant shall be disqualified.

General Health: Candidate must be physically and mentally fit to perform duty in any part of the world, in any climate and terrain. They must conform to normal anatomy without loss or deformity of any appendages, and be free from active, latent, acute, or chronic medical or surgical disability, infection, or skin ailments.

faqs.question: What is the designation and stream of this recruitment in the Indian Air Force?
faqs.answer: The recruitment is for joining the Indian Air Force as Agniveervayu (Musician) under Intake 01/2027.

faqs.question: What are the online registration dates for IAF Agniveervayu Musician?
faqs.answer: The online registration starts on 20 July 2026 at 11:00 AM and closes on 02 August 2026 at 11:00 PM (23:00 Hr).

faqs.question: When and where will the recruitment rally be held?
faqs.answer: The recruitment rally will be held from 31 August 2026 to 09 September 2026. The venues are 2 ASC C/O Race Course Camp, Air Force Station New Delhi and 7 ASC, No. 1 Cubbon Road, Bengaluru.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this Agniveervayu Musician intake?
faqs.answer: Only unmarried Indian male and female candidates who possess the required 10th/Matriculation qualification and the specified music ability and experience certification are eligible.

faqs.question: What is the required date of birth block for candidates?
faqs.answer: Candidates must be born between 01 January 2005 and 01 July 2009 (both dates inclusive). In any case, the upper age limit as on the date of enrolment must be 22 years.

faqs.question: What are the educational qualifications required for this post?
faqs.answer: Candidates must have passed Matriculation/10th or equivalent with minimum pass marks from any Central, State, or UT Government recognized School/Board as on the date of registration.

faqs.question: What music proficiency is mandatory for the selection?
faqs.answer: Candidates must have proficiency in music with accuracy in tempo, pitch, and singing one complete song. They should be able to perform one preparatory tune, read notations, tune individual instruments, and play an instrument from List A or List B.

faqs.question: What are the music instruments listed in List A and List B?
faqs.answer: List A includes wind/brass/orchestral instruments (Concert Flute/Piccolo, Oboe, Clarinet, Saxophone, French Horn, Trumpet, Trombone, Baritone, Euphonium, Bass/Tuba). List B includes keyboards, string, classical, and percussion instruments (Keyboard/Organ/Piano, Guitar, Violin, Viola, String Bass, Percussion/Drums, and All Indian Classical Instruments).

faqs.question: Is a music experience certificate mandatory? What are the accepted certificates?
faqs.answer: Yes, candidates must possess one of the following: (1) Grade 5th or above from Trinity College London (TCL), Royal Schools of Music (RSM), etc., (2) Diploma in music for Hindustani/Carnatic from a recognized university, or (3) Participation/Award certificate at various events (with blowing instrument performance with staff notation).

faqs.question: What is the monthly pay package and allowances for Agniveervayu?
faqs.answer: Agniveervayu will receive ₹30,000/- in the 1st year, ₹33,000/- in the 2nd year, ₹36,500/- in the 3rd year, and ₹40,000/- in the 4th year. Risk, hardship, dress, and travel allowances are paid in addition to perks like ration, clothing, accommodation, and medical facilities.

faqs.question: What is the Seva Nidhi package paid upon completion of service?
faqs.answer: After completing 4 years of engagement, candidates receive a one-time "Seva Nidhi" package totaling approximately ₹10.04 Lakhs (excluding interest), which includes their accumulated monthly contributions (₹5.02 Lakhs) and a matching contribution from the Government.

faqs.question: Is there any pension or gratuity after 4 years of service?
faqs.answer: No, Agniveervayu enrolled under this scheme are not entitled to any gratuity or pensionary benefits. They are governed by the Agnipath scheme rules.

faqs.question: Is there any life insurance coverage provided?
faqs.answer: Yes, a non-contributory Life Insurance cover of ₹48 Lakhs is provided to Agniveervayu for the entire duration of their engagement in the Indian Air Force.

faqs.question: What is the registration fee and how can it be paid?
faqs.answer: The registration fee is ₹100/- plus 18% GST (non-refundable). It can be paid online through Net Banking, Debit Cards, Credit Cards, or UPI via the integrated payment gateway.

faqs.question: What is the sequence of the selection tests during the rally?
faqs.answer: The sequence is: (1) Scrutiny of original certificates, (2) Physical Fitness Test (PFT-I: 1.6 Kms run; PFT-II: Push-ups, sit-ups, squats), (3) English Written Test, (4) Music Proficiency Test (MPT), and (5) Medical Examination.

faqs.question: What are the timing standards for the 1.6 Kms run in PFT-I?
faqs.answer: Male candidates must complete the 1.6 Kms run within 7 minutes, and female candidates must complete it within 8 minutes.

faqs.question: What are the PFT-II physical exercise requirements for male and female candidates?
faqs.answer: Male candidates must do 10 push-ups (1 min), 10 sit-ups (1 min), and 20 squats (1 min). Female candidates must do 10 sit-ups (1 min 30 sec) and 15 squats (1 min).

faqs.question: What is the pattern of the English Written Test?
faqs.answer: The test consists of 30 objective-type multiple-choice questions (MCQs) based on CBSE 10th/Matriculation syllabus. The exam duration is 30 minutes, and there is no negative marking.

faqs.question: How is the final merit prepared for enrolment?
faqs.answer: The final merit list is prepared in order of performance in selection tests (Written & Music tests) and medical fitness, subject to vacancy availability. Enrolment in regular cadre as an Airman is offered to up to 25% of each batch after 4 years.

faqs.question: Are permanent body tattoos permitted?
faqs.answer: Permanent tattoos are only permitted on the inner face of the forearms, back of the hand/reverse palm, or traditional tribal tattoos. Offensive, sexist, or racist tattoos are strictly prohibited regardless of location. Postcard-size photos of accepted tattoos must be submitted.

faqs.question: What are the visual and refractive error standards?
faqs.answer: Visual acuity must be 6/12 each eye, correctable to 6/6. Refractive error limits are Hypermetropia up to +2.0D and Myopia up to -1D (including ± 0.50D Astigmatism). Colour vision must be CP-II. History of LASIK/PRK is NOT accepted.

faqs.question: Can female candidates apply? Are there any specific terms for them?
faqs.answer: Yes, unmarried female candidates are eligible. They must undertake not to get married or get pregnant during the 4-year engagement period. Pregnancy will debar them from regular cadre selection and make them liable for dismissal.

faqs.question: What unique passport photo requirement is specified for the online application?
faqs.answer: The passport photo (size 100KB-200KB, under 1 month old) must be taken with the candidate holding a black slate in front of his/her chest with his/her name and date of photo taken clearly written on it with white chalk in capital letters.

faqs.question: Are candidates currently employed in Government jobs eligible? Is an NOC required?
faqs.answer: Yes, they are eligible, but they must apply under intimation to their employer, and mandatorily submit an original No Objection Certificate (NOC) at the time of the Skill Test/Rally.

faqs.question: Who can be contacted for queries or technical assistance regarding the application?
faqs.answer: For help desk queries, candidates can call +91-9513253233 (Mon-Sat, 09:00 AM to 06:00 PM) or CASB at 011-25694209 / 25699606. Queries can also be emailed to iafrecruitment@edcil.co.in.

topics: Engineering Mechanics: Free-body diagrams and equilibrium; trusses and frames; virtual work; kinematics and dynamics of particles and of rigid bodies in plane motion; impulse and momentum (linear and angular) and energy formulations, collisions.

Mechanics of Materials: Stress and strain, elastic constants, Poisson's ratio; Mohr's circle for plane stress and plane strain; thin cylinders; shear force and bending moment diagrams; bending and shear stresses; deflection of beams; torsion of circular shafts; Euler's theory of columns; energy methods; thermal stresses; strain gauges and rosettes; testing of materials with universal testing machine; testing of hardness and impact strength.

Theory of Machines: Displacement, velocity and acceleration analysis of plane mechanisms; dynamic analysis of linkages; cams; gears and gear trains; flywheels and governors; balancing of reciprocating and rotating masses; gyroscope.
Vibrations: Free and forced vibration of single degree of freedom systems, effect of damping; vibration isolation; resonance; critical speeds of shafts.

Machine Design: Design for static and dynamic loading; failure theories; fatigue strength and the S-N diagram; principles of the design of machine elements such as bolted, riveted and welded joints; shafts, gears, rolling and sliding contact bearings, brakes and clutches, springs.

Fluid Mechanics: Fluid properties; fluid statics, manometry, buoyancy, forces on submerged bodies, stability of floating bodies; control-volume analysis of mass, momentum and energy; fluid acceleration; differential equations of continuity and momentum; Bernoulli's equation; dimensional analysis; viscous flow of incompressible fluids, boundary layer, elementary turbulent flow, flow through pipes, head losses in pipes, bends and fittings.

Heat-Transfer: Modes of heat transfer; one dimensional heat conduction, resistance concept and electrical analogy, heat transfer through fins; unsteady heat conduction, lumped parameter system, Heisler's charts; thermal boundary layer, dimensionless parameters in free and forced convective heat transfer, heat transfer correlations for flow over flat plates and through pipes, effect of turbulence; heat exchanger performance, LMTD and NTU methods; radiative heat transfer, Stefan-Boltzmann law, Wien's displacement law, black and grey surfaces, view factors, radiation network analysis.

Thermodynamics: Thermodynamic systems and processes; properties of pure substances, behaviour of ideal and real gases; zeroth and first laws of thermodynamics, calculation of work and heat in various processes; second law of thermodynamics; thermodynamic property charts and tables, availability and irreversibility; thermodynamic relations.

Applications: Power Engineering (Air and gas compressors; vapour and gas power cycles, concepts of regeneration and reheat), I.C. Engines (Air-standard Otto, Diesel and dual cycles), Refrigeration and Air-conditioning (Vapour and gas refrigeration and heat pump cycles; properties of moist air, psychrometric chart, basic psychrometric processes), Turbomachinery (Impulse and reaction principles, velocity diagrams, Pelton-wheel, Francis and Kaplan turbines).

Engineering Materials: Structure and properties of engineering materials, phase diagrams, heat treatment, stress-strain diagrams for engineering materials. Elasticity, plasticity, fracture and fracture toughness, fatigue, solid solutions, equilibrium diagram, thermal treatment, TTT and CCT diagrams. Cooling curves, austempering, martempering, factors affecting hardenability, function of alloying elements in steel.

Casting, Forming and Joining Processes: Different types of castings, design of patterns, moulds and cores; solidification and cooling; riser and gating design. Plastic deformation and yield criteria; fundamentals of hot and cold working processes; load estimation for bulk (forging, rolling, extrusion, drawing) and sheet (shearing, deep drawing, bending) metal forming processes; principles of powder metallurgy. Principles of welding, brazing, soldering and adhesive bonding.

Machining and Machine Tool Operations: Mechanics of machining; basic machine tools; single and multi-point cutting tools, tool geometry and materials, tool life and wear; economics of machining; principles of non-traditional machining processes; principles of work holding, design of jigs and fixtures.

Metrology and Inspection: Limits, fits and tolerances; linear and angular measurements; comparators; gauge design; interferometry; form and finish measurement; alignment and testing methods; tolerance analysis in manufacturing and assembly.
Computer Integrated Manufacturing: Basic concepts of CAD/CAM and their integration tools.
Production Planning and Control: Forecasting models, aggregate production planning, scheduling, materials requirement planning.
Inventory Control: Deterministic models; safety stock inventory control systems.
Operations Research: Linear programming, simplex method, transportation, assignment, network flow models, simple queuing models, PERT and CPM.

Manufacturing Processes: Metal casting patterns and moulds; casting defects and repair; hot, warm and cold working of metals; soldering, brazing and welding; welding metallurgy, defects in welded joints; NDT using dye-penetrant, ultrasonic, radiography, eddy current, acoustic emission and magnetic particle methods.

Testing of Material: Non-destructive testing (Ultrasonic testing, radiography, magnetic particle testing, eddy current testing, dye penetration testing). Physical testing (Tensile test, % elongation, % reduction in area, hardness Brinell/Rockwell/Vickers, impact test Izod/charpy, bend test, shear test, fatigue test, creep test).
Chemical Testing: Ferrous and non-ferrous metals. Metallography; micro and macro examination. Testing of paints, rubber, textiles, wood, and plastics.
Material Science: Thermal, chemical, electrical, magnetic and mechanical properties. Structure of metals, solid solution, diffusion, transformation, deformation, corrosion.
Air Compressors & AC: Types of air compressors, performance, receivers, intercoolers, after coolers. Air conditioning units and plants, types, selection of plants.

faqs.question: What is the official Advertisement or Vacancy Circular Number for this recruitment?
faqs.answer: The vacancy circular number is VC No. RG/11/26.

faqs.question: What is the designation/post name and number of vacancies?
faqs.answer: The post is Assistant Manager (Mechanical) and there are 24 vacancies in total.

faqs.question: What is the category-wise vacancy distribution?
faqs.answer: The 24 vacancies are distributed as: UR: 12, SC: 5, ST: 4, EWS: 2, OBC (NCL): 1, PwBD: 1.

faqs.question: What is the essential academic qualification required for Assistant Manager (Mechanical)?
faqs.answer: Candidates must possess a full-time Bachelor’s Degree (B.E/B.Tech/B.Sc Engg) in Mechanical Engineering/Technology in Mechanical, Production, Production & Industrial, Manufacturing, Mechanical/Railways, Mechatronics, or Automobile (or any combination of these in part or whole).

faqs.question: What is the minimum post-qualification experience required?
faqs.answer: A minimum of 2 years of post-qualification outdoor work experience in the field of production, mechanical maintenance, or other mechanical engineering areas is required. The candidate must have worked at a project site, factory, or plant during this period.

faqs.question: What is the maximum age limit for applying and the cut-off date?
faqs.answer: The maximum age limit is 32 years. The cut-off date to determine age, experience, and eligibility is 17.08.2026.

faqs.question: What is the scale of pay for Assistant Manager (Mechanical) in RITES?
faqs.answer: The scale of pay is INR 40,000 - 1,40,000 (regular basis).

faqs.question: What is the application fee for different categories?
faqs.answer: General and OBC candidates pay Rs. 600/- plus applicable taxes. EWS, SC, ST, and PwBD candidates pay Rs. 300/- plus applicable taxes.

faqs.question: Is the application fee refundable for SC/ST/PwBD candidates?
faqs.answer: Yes, the fee paid by SC/ST/PwBD candidates will be refunded upon their participation in the written exam / interview, after deducting GST and bank charges.

faqs.question: What are the written test centers for RITES AM Mechanical?
faqs.answer: The written test will be conducted at 6 locations: Delhi/Gurgaon, Kolkata, Bangalore, Mumbai, Guwahati, and Bhubaneswar.

faqs.question: Does RITES have a negative marking system in the Written Test?
faqs.answer: No, there is no negative marking system applicable. No marks are deducted for incorrect answers.

faqs.question: What is the duration of the Written Test?
faqs.answer: The Written Test consists of 125 objective questions and has a duration of 2.5 hours (150 minutes).

faqs.question: Are PwBD candidates eligible for extra time in the exam?
faqs.answer: Yes, candidates belonging to PwBD category are eligible for a compensatory time of 50 minutes.

faqs.question: What is the minimum qualifying marks in the Written Test?
faqs.answer: The minimum qualifying marks are 50% for UR/EWS (62.5 marks out of 125) and 45% for SC/ST/OBC(NCL)/PwBD candidates against reserved posts (56.25 marks out of 125).

faqs.question: In what ratio will candidates be called for the interview?
faqs.answer: Candidates will be called for interview in the ratio of 1:6 to the number of vacancies based on Written Test merit.

faqs.question: What is the marks weightage distribution for selection?
faqs.answer: Written Test carries 60% weightage, and Personal Interview carries 40% weightage (Technical & Professional proficiency: 30 marks; Personality Communication & Competency: 10 marks).

faqs.question: What are the minimum qualifying marks in the Interview?
faqs.answer: A minimum of 60% marks for UR/EWS (24 marks out of 40) and 50% for SC/ST/OBC(NCL)/PwBD against reserved posts (20 marks out of 40) is required in the interview.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum aggregate mark required to be on the panel?
faqs.answer: No, there are no minimum qualifying marks required in the aggregate. Only qualifying in written test and interview individually is required.

faqs.question: Can candidates choose the medium/language of the selection process?
faqs.answer: Yes, candidates have the option to appear for the selection process (written test and/or interview) either in Hindi or English.

faqs.question: Is training/internship counted as work experience?
faqs.answer: No. Training (except on-the-job training), internships, teaching, academic, fellowship, or PhD research experience shall NOT be counted as experience. However, Apprenticeship training as per the Apprenticeship Act 1961 is counted.

faqs.question: What is the duration of probation for selected candidates?
faqs.answer: The probation period is initially for one year from the date of joining.

faqs.question: What is the cut-off date of acquiring the educational qualification?
faqs.answer: The date of acquiring qualification will be the earliest of: (i) last day of month of final exam, (ii) date of declaration of result, (iii) date of marksheet issuance, (iv) date of degree certificate issuance.

faqs.question: Are candidates required to send hard copies of applications to RITES office?
faqs.answer: No, hard copies must NOT be sent through post or courier. Scanned copies of all documents must be uploaded online.

faqs.question: What are the contact details for fee payment queries?
faqs.answer: Candidates can contact the HDFC Helpdesk at 011-33557000 (Extension: 13221) or email pg.service@hdfc.bank.in.

faqs.question: Where can candidates send general recruitment queries?
faqs.answer: Queries can be emailed to rectt@rites.com including VC No, Registration No, Full Name, and valid email address.

cert-in-scientist-b-2026.seoDescription: CERT-In Recruitment 2026: Apply online for 133 Scientist B (Group A) vacancies under MeitY. Direct recruitment based on GATE 2024/2025/2026 scores. Check eligibility, vacancies, and interview details.
cert-in-scientist-b-2026.lsiKeywords: CERT-In Recruitment 2026, Scientist B Vacancy, GATE 2024 2025 2026, MeitY Careers, Cyber Security Jobs India, CERT-In Scientist-B Syllabus
cert-in-scientist-b-2026.title: Scientist-B – 133 Posts
cert-in-scientist-b-2026.jobLocation: Any place in India or outside India in the interest of the Organization
overview: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In or ICERT), under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, is the national nodal agency for performing functions in the area of cybersecurity. Established in 2004 under the IT Amendment Act 2008, CERT-In commands high prestige in securing the country’s cyber infrastructure.

CERT-In has issued a detailed advertisement (Advt.No: CERT-In/SCB/2026/1) for direct recruitment to the post of Scientist-'B' (equivalent to Group-'A' level-10, pay scale Rs. 56,100 to Rs. 1,77,500 of the 7th CPC). A total of 133 vacancies are open across three major disciplines: Computer Science and Information Technology (CS), Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DA), and Electronics and Communication Engineering (EC).

Eligible candidates will be shortlisted for a Personal Interaction/Interview based on their valid Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE) score from the years 2024, 2025, or 2026. The aggregate merit will be calculated with 60% weightage on the GATE score and 40% weightage on the Personal Interaction/Interview. Online applications are accepted from 14/07/2026 to 17/08/2026 (05:30 PM). Application fees are NIL for all categories.
No work experience is required for this recruitment, making it an exceptional opportunity for engineering graduates and postgraduates to directly join a core national security agency.

Or Master's in Science: Computer Science, Computer Application, Computer and Network Security.

For Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DA): Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or Technology OR Master's Degree in Science disciplines OR Master's in Computer Application (MCA) in relevant subject disciplines.

Approved DA subject disciplines: Software System, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Informatics, Information System, Information Security, Computer Management, Cyber Law, Information Science, Computational Linguistics, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Cyber Security, Computer & Info Science, Cyber Law & Info Security, Advance Network, Computational Science, Cryptography, Machine Learning, Cloud Security, Digital Forensics, Big Data Analytics, IoT, Quantum Computing, Blockchain Technology.

Facilities like CGHS are not available, but a separate comprehensive medical policy exists for ICERT Employees.

selectionProcess.description: Candidates must successfully submit their online application before 17.08.2026. Credentials and uploaded certificates are screened for basic eligibility criteria.

Eligible candidates are shortlisted for the interview based on their GATE Score (highest score amongst 2024, 2025, or 2026). Shortlisting is done in the ratio of 1:5 per vacancy, discipline-wise and category-wise.
Before attending the interview, candidates must undergo thorough verification of original documents. Non-production of original certificates or any discrepancy results in immediate disqualification.

selectionProcess.description: On the day of interview, candidates must validate their GATE scores by logging into the official GATE results portal in front of the verification board.

Candidates are assessed on technical/academic knowledge (based on their qualifying degree), presentation, communication skills, comprehension, and academic performance (0.05 marks per percentage in the qualifying degree).
The final selection merit is compiled by aggregating 60% weightage of the GATE score and 40% weightage of marks obtained in the Personal Interaction/Interview.

examPattern.negativeMarking: No written examination will be conducted by CERT-In. Shortlisting is strictly based on valid GATE 2024/2025/2026 scores. Therefore, no negative marking rules apply.

reservation.title: Reservation, Relaxation & Category Concessions
detailsList: Reservation benefits are admissible to SC, ST, OBC-NCL, EWS, and PwBD categories strictly in accordance with Central Government rules and against posts reserved for them.

OBC-NCL Certificate Requirement: Candidates must submit a copy of a valid OBC (NCL) certificate in the prescribed format (Annexure II) issued during the Financial Year 2026-27 (on or after 01.04.2026) by a competent authority, proving they do not belong to the Creamy Layer.

EWS Certificate Requirement: Candidates must produce a valid EWS Income & Asset Certificate in prescribed format (Annexure III) issued for the Financial Year 2025-26 (valid for 2026-27) based on gross annual family income below Rs. 8 Lakh and asset criteria.

PwBD horizontal reservation of 5 vacancies total (3 in CS, 1 in DA, 1 in EC) is applicable for candidates with at least 40% permanent disability. A valid permanent disability certificate from a Government Medical Board is required (Annexure IV/V/VI).

examCentres.title: Interview Venue & Selection Locations
examCentres.details: The document verification and Personal Interaction/Interview of shortlisted candidates will be conducted at Delhi or at any other location/mode approved by the competent authority. The exact date, time, and venue details will be provided in the Interview Call Letters downloadable from the official portal. No request for postponement or change in location/mode will be entertained, and no TA/DA will be paid by CERT-In for attending the process.

howToApply: Step 1: Registration – Candidates must visit the official CERT-In website (https://www.cert-in.org.in) and register online using a valid email ID and mobile number between 14/07/2026 and 17/08/2026.

Step 2: Fill online Application Form & Uploading documents – Log in with generated credentials, fill in personal details, educational qualifications, GATE details, and upload legible self-attested scanned documents (checklist 5.1 in PDF format, size 10KB to 500KB) and recent photograph/signature.

Step 3: Download Confirmation Page – Carefully review the filled details. After ensuring correctness, submit the form. Download and print the Confirmation Page containing the Application Number for future reference.

overview: National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) is a Joint Sector Company of Government of India and participating State Governments formed for the implementation of the High Speed Train Corridor Project in India. This is one of the most ambitious projects in the Rail infrastructure sector, designed to boost the Indian economy and construct the first-ever high-speed bullet train rail corridor between Mumbai and Ahmedabad.

NHSRCL has released an official recruitment notification for the posts of Technician under Vacancy Notice Nos. 35/2026 to 49/2026. This recruitment is conducted on an Absorption Basis in the IDA Pay scale of Rs. 35,000 to Rs. 1,10,000 (NE-2) for regular and contractual employees who are currently serving in the Operations & Maintenance departments of Indian Railways, government-owned or operated Railways, Metro Railways, or RRTS.

There are a total of 237 vacancies distributed across Civil/Track, Electrical, Signalling & Telecom, and Rolling Stock domains. Freshers with higher educational qualifications like BE/B.Tech without holding the prerequisite ITI or Diploma are explicitly ineligible to apply. Experience and age limits will be reckoned as on 30th June 2026.

faqs.question: What is the full form of NHSRCL?
faqs.answer: NHSRCL stands for National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited.

faqs.question: What is the role of NHSRCL?
faqs.answer: NHSRCL is a Joint Sector Company of the Government of India and participating State Governments formed for the implementation of High Speed Train Corridor Projects in India, including the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project.

faqs.question: What are the post names and total vacancies under this advertisement?
faqs.answer: The posts are for Technician across different disciplines with a total of 237 vacancies.

faqs.question: What are the advertisement vacancy notice numbers for these posts?
faqs.answer: The vacancy notice numbers range from 35/2026 to 49/2026.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for these Technician posts?
faqs.answer: Only regular or contractual employees currently working in the Operations & Maintenance (O&M) departments of Indian Railways, Government-owned or operated Railways, Metro Railways, or RRTS systems are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: What is the minimum experience required for NHSRCL Technician posts?
faqs.answer: A minimum of 02 years of post-qualification experience in the relevant field within the O&M departments of Indian Railways, Government-owned or operated Railways, Metro, or RRTS is required.

faqs.question: What is the crucial date for reckoning experience, qualification, and age?
faqs.answer: The experience and other eligibility criteria will be reckoned as on 30th June 2026.

faqs.question: Are B.E. / B.Tech degree holders eligible to apply without ITI or Diploma?
faqs.answer: No. Candidates having higher qualifications (e.g., BE/BTech) but who do not possess the basic ITI or Diploma qualification in the respective discipline are strictly NOT eligible.

faqs.question: What is the IDA Pay scale for Technician (NE-2) posts in NHSRCL?
faqs.answer: The pay scale is Rs. 35,000 - Rs. 1,10,000 (NE-2).

faqs.question: What is the maximum age limit for applying to NHSRCL Technician vacancies?
faqs.answer: The maximum age limit is 35 years as on 30th June 2026.

faqs.question: What are the medical standards required for these posts?
faqs.answer: Candidates must meet the Bee-one (B-1) medical standards.

faqs.question: Where is the place of posting for selected technicians?
faqs.answer: Selected candidates can be posted anywhere in the NHSRCL/MAHSR (Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail) Project.

faqs.question: What is the application fee for UR, EWS, and OBC candidates?
faqs.answer: The non-refundable application fee is Rs. 400/- (exclusive of transaction processing charges).

faqs.question: Which categories are exempted from paying the application fee?
faqs.answer: Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and Women candidates are completely exempted from payment of the application fee.

faqs.question: Can a candidate apply for multiple Technician posts?
faqs.answer: No. Candidates can only apply against any one of the posts from vacancy notice nos. 35/2026 to 49/2026. Only one application is permitted, and the CBT for all these posts may be held on the same day and time.

faqs.question: What is the selection process for NHSRCL Technicians?
faqs.answer: The selection process consists of three stages: (1) Computer Based Test (CBT), (2) Document Verification, and (3) Medical Examination.

faqs.question: Is there a probation period after appointment?
faqs.answer: Yes, candidates appointed on an absorption basis will be on probation for a period of one (01) year.

faqs.question: Is there any Surety Bond required to join NHSRCL?
faqs.answer: Yes. Candidates must execute a surety bond of Rs. 3,00,000/- to serve the corporation for a minimum of 4 years. If training is imparted, they must execute a surety bond for the Cost of Training and serve for a minimum of 6 years after completion of training.

faqs.question: Does the work involve shift duties?
faqs.answer: Yes. The work predominantly involves shift duties, night-shift maintenance activities, and emergency restoration works as per HSR operational requirements.

faqs.question: What is required as proof of experience?
faqs.answer: Candidates must submit a Competency Certificate or Experience Certificate issued by their employer, which clearly indicates year-wise details of the nature and type of work performed.

faqs.question: Is teaching or apprenticeship experience considered as part of required years of experience?
faqs.answer: No. Experience from teaching, faculty roles, apprenticeships, internships, proprietorships, partnerships, or freelancing will NOT be considered as part of the required years of experience.

overview: The Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM) is an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India. The Council carries out its pioneering research, clinical trials, and healthcare delivery functions through its extensive network of 24 peripheral institutes, centers, and hospitals spread across the country, guided by its main headquarters in New Delhi. This is an exceptional career opportunity for medical professionals, scientific researchers, administrative personnel, and support staff to serve in a premier national body.

CCRUM has released its highly detailed Vacancy Advertisement No. 01/2026 inviting online applications from eligible Indian citizens for recruitment to a wide range of Group 'A', 'B', and 'C' positions. A total of 179 regular vacancies have been announced. These vacancies span diverse specializations including Research Officers, Assistant Research Officers, Staff Nurses, Accounts Officers, Research Assistants, Library Assistants, Laboratory Technologists, Clerks (UDC, LDC), Pharmacists, Drivers, and Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS).

The recruitment features an offline-exempt fee payment structure where women, SC, ST, PwBD, EWS, and Ex-Servicemen categories are exempted from paying the examination fee, only requiring a Rs. 500/- processing fee. The selection process will be conducted via an online Computer-Based Test (CBT), accompanied by a Personal Interview for Group 'A' posts and qualifying practical skill tests (typing, shorthand, driving, or translation) for several Group 'B' and 'C' vacancies. The registration and fee portal will remain active from 1st July 2026 until 31st July 2026, followed by a dedicated modification window in August.

All interested candidates are strongly advised to thoroughly review the official notification details regarding educational qualifications, age limits, post-specific experience criteria, reservation rules, and exam patterns before submitting their online profiles on the Council's web portal. Candidates can apply for multiple posts separately provided they meet the requisite criteria for each selected role.
