education: Essential Educational Qualifications and Experience Required for Vacant Posts:
Group-A Research Officer Posts:

1. Research Officer (Unani): Post Graduate Degree (MD or MS) in Unani System of Medicine from any NCISM (formerly CCIM) recognized University/Institution. Plus, mandatory enrolment on the Central Register of NCISM/CCIM or State Register of Unani/ISM.
2. Research Officer (Pathology): M.D. in Pathology from an MCI (now NMC) recognized University or Institution. Mandatory enrolment on the Central Register of MCI or State Register of Medical Council.

3. Research Officer (Physiology): Master's Degree in Molecular Biology, Biotechnology, Human Genetics, or Genetics Engineering from a recognized University or Institution. Candidates must possess either 3 years of post-qualification experience in relevant subject in recognized research/academic institution/lab/industry, OR a Ph.D. degree in the concerned subject after Master's.
Group-B Officer and Technical Posts:
4. Assistant Research Officer (Pharmacology): M.Sc in Pharmacology or M.V.Sc Degree from a recognized University or Institution, with a proven aptitude for research.

5. Assistant Research Officer (Pharmacognosy/Botany): Master's Degree in the concerned discipline from a recognized University or Institution. Candidates must have 3 years of research or teaching experience after obtaining Master's degree, OR a Ph.D. in the concerned discipline.

6. Staff Nurse: B.Sc. (Hons) in Nursing, Regular B.Sc. Nursing, or Post-Basic B.Sc. Nursing from a recognized University or Institute; must be registered as a Nurse or Nurse & Mid-wife (RN or RN & RM) with the State Nursing Council. OR, GNM Diploma with RN/RN & RM registration with the State Nursing Council and at least 01 year of post-qualification experience in a minimum 50-bedded hospital.

7. Accounts Officer (HQ): Degree from a recognized University or Institution, with 3 years of experience in Cash, Accounts, and Budget work in a Government Office, PSU, Autonomous Body, or Statutory Body.

8. Research Assistant (Chemistry / Botany): Post Graduate Degree in the concerned discipline (M.Sc. Chemistry / M.Sc. Botany) from a recognized University or Institution, with a proven aptitude for research.

9. Investigator (Statistics): Master's Degree in Statistics or Mathematics with Statistics as one of the subjects from a recognized University. Candidates must have 3 years of experience in statistical work involving collection, compilation, interpretation, and analysis of statistical data, OR a Ph.D. in Statistics.

10. Medical Laboratory Technologist (MLT): Bachelor's Degree in Medical Laboratory Science from a recognized University or Institute with at least 02 years of relevant post-qualification laboratory experience.
11. Library & Information Assistant (LIA): Degree from a recognized university and a separate Degree in Library Science from a recognized University or Institution.

12. Proof Reader: Degree from a recognized university, and a 1-year Diploma in Books Publishing/Production, Printing Technology, or Marketing, with 3 years of post-qualification experience in the publishing line.

13. Hindi Assistant: Degree from a recognized university with adequate knowledge of Hindi equal to Hindi standard B.A. examination of an Indian University. Ability to translate from English to Hindi and vice-versa, as evidenced by a translation test. OR, Post Graduate qualification in Hindi with translation ability.
Group-C Technical & Clerical Posts:

14. Pharmacist: 10+2 with Science subjects from a recognized Board/Institution. Must have a 2-year Diploma in Pharmacy from a recognized Institution and be registered with the State/Central Pharmacy Council.
15. Social Worker: Degree from a recognized University, and a Diploma in Social Work with 1 year of experience in social work in recognized institutions/hospitals; OR a Master's Degree in Sociology.

16. Radiographer: 10+2 with Science subjects from a recognized Board. Must have a 2-year Diploma/Certificate in Radiography and 1 year of post-qualification radiography experience in a recognized hospital or medical institute.

17. Compounder: Matriculation (10th) or equivalent. Must possess a Certificate of training as a Compounder in Unani System of Medicine of minimum 1 year duration from a recognized institution, and 2 years of experience preferably in a Unani Dispensary or Hospital.

18. Stenographer Grade-III: Matriculation (10th) or equivalent from a recognized Board. Shorthand speed of 80 words per minute and typing speed of 40 words per minute on a computer. Must have working knowledge of computer handling.
19. Upper Division Clerk (UDC): Degree from a recognized University or equivalent qualification.

20. Lower Division Clerk (LDC): 12th Class or equivalent qualification from a recognized Board. Must possess a typing speed of 35 words per minute in English or 30 words per minute in Hindi on a computer.

21. Staff Car Driver: Matriculation (10th) pass. Must possess a valid driving license for Motor Cars / LMV, have 3 years of driving experience, and have basic knowledge of motor mechanism (able to remove minor vehicle defects).
22. Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS): Matriculation (10th) pass from a recognized board, OR ITI pass in a relevant subject.

selectionProcess.description: Candidates for all Group A, B, and C posts must appear in an online Computer Based Test. For Group B & C, the CBT carries 100 marks. For Group A, the CBT carries 70 marks. The test questions will be bilingual (English & Hindi) and will have 0.25 negative marking for each wrong answer (except MTS, which has no negative marking).

Candidates for Group-A Research Officer posts who qualify in the CBT exam will be shortlisted for a Personal Interview carrying 30 marks. Shortlisting ratios will be: 1:5 for 1 vacancy, 1:4 for 2 vacancies, and 1:3 for 3 and more vacancies.

Mandatory qualifying skill tests will be held for specific posts: (1) LDC: typing test at 35 wpm in English or 30 wpm in Hindi on computer; (2) Stenographer Grade-III: shorthand dictation test at 80 wpm for 10 minutes and transcription on computer; (3) Staff Car Driver: driving and minor motor mechanism test; (4) Hindi Assistant: English-to-Hindi and Hindi-to-English translation test.

Biometric registration (Right Thumb Impression) and digital photo capturing of candidates will be performed at test centers prior to the exam, at the end of the exam, and during document verification.

Merit-listed candidates who qualify in the CBT and respective skill tests will be called for document verification of original certificates, experience letters, caste certificates, and NoC from existing employers.
Final selection and institute-wise allotment will be decided on a merit-cum-preference basis as per vacancies across different States and peripheral centers.

howToApply: Step 1: Registration — Visit the official website www.ccrum.res.in or www.ccrum.ayush.gov.in and click on the 'Advertisement/Vacancy' tab. Click on 'Online Application Submission' link to open the registration portal. Click on Sign-up/Create Account to enter basic details: Full Name, Father Name, Mother Name, Gender, Date of Birth, Mobile Number, E-Mail ID, and a valid Govt. ID Proof (Voter ID, Passport, PAN, or Driving License). Confirm mobile & email via OTP.

Step 2: Profile Completion — Log in using the system-generated login credentials. Complete the profile fields with demographic, category, sub-category details, and add basic qualification details (SSC, HSC, Diploma, Degree, etc.).

Step 3: Document Upload — Upload scanned passport size colour photograph (taken/clicked in 2026, size 50-100 KB in JPEG/JPG format, straight look, no hat/cap/dark glasses except religious headwear) and scanned signature (using Black ink pen on white paper, size 50-100 KB in JPG/JPEG). Upload other relevant certificates (Caste, PwBD, ESM, Educational marksheets) in PDF/JPG format, sized 100 KB to 1000 KB.
Step 4: Profile Review & Submission — Preview the profile information. Click on the undertaking checkbox to confirm correctness. Once submitted, profile details CANNOT be changed at any stage.

Step 5: Apply for Post & Fee Payment — Click on 'Apply for Post' tab. Select the post(s) you wish to apply for, fill in post-specific details, and proceed to upload post-specific documents. Once verified, you will be redirected to the online payment gateway to pay processing/exam fee via Debit/Credit Card, Net Banking, or UPI.

Step 6: Print Confirmation — After successful fee payment, the transaction status will update to 'Payment Received'. Download the system-generated e-mail confirmation and print out the application form sheet with the Payment Receipt for future reference.

reservation.title: Reservation & Category-wise Relaxation Rules
detailsList: SC/ST & OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) reservations are applicable as per Central Government of India guidelines.
OBC Certificate and Non-Creamy Layer status certificate must be obtained within 3 years before the closing date of application.
EWS candidates must have a gross annual family income below Rs. 8 Lakhs and must not possess specified agricultural land or residential flats.
Vacancies earmarked for EWS, if not filled due to non-availability of suitable candidates, shall not be carried forward as backlog and will be placed in the next recruitment year.
Ex-Servicemen (ESM) horizontal reservation is applicable for Group C posts: 3 posts in UDC, 1 in Stenographer, 2 in LDC, and 4 in MTS.
PwBD candidates with 40% or more disability are eligible for reservation benefits and scribe facility as per Ministry of Social Justice guidelines.
Maximum cumulative age limit after combining all age relaxations shall not exceed 56 years under any circumstances.

faqs.question: What is the recruiting organization and advertisement number for this recruitment?
faqs.answer: Organization: Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM), Ministry of Ayush, Govt. of India. Advertisement Number: 1/2026.

faqs.question: What are the key dates for applying to the CCRUM recruitment?
faqs.answer: Online application starts on 1st July 2026 at 10:00 hours, and closes on 31st July 2026 at 23:59 hours. The modification window opens on 3rd August 2026 at 10:00 hours and closes on 5th August 2026 at 23:59 hours.

faqs.question: What is the total number of vacancies advertised across different posts?
faqs.answer: A total of 179 vacancies are advertised across 23 different Group A, B, and C posts.

faqs.question: What is the application mode for this recruitment?
faqs.answer: The application mode is strictly ONLINE. No physical/hard copy applications will be accepted.

faqs.question: What are the Group A posts available in this recruitment?
faqs.answer: Research Officer (Unani) - 16 posts; Research Officer (Pathology) - 2 posts; and Research Officer (Physiology) - 1 post.

faqs.question: What is the salary or pay level for the Group A Research Officer posts?
faqs.answer: They are placed in Pay Level 10 of the 7th CPC (Rs. 56,100 - Rs. 1,77,500). Research Officer (Unani) is also eligible for NPA as per Govt rules.

faqs.question: What are the essential educational qualifications for a Staff Nurse?
faqs.answer: B.Sc. (Hons) in Nursing, Regular B.Sc. Nursing, or Post-Basic B.Sc. Nursing from a recognized University/Institute, with RN or RN&RM registration; OR GNM Diploma with RN/RN&RM registration and 1 year experience in a minimum 50-bedded hospital.

faqs.question: What is the upper age limit for the Staff Nurse post?
faqs.answer: The upper age limit is not exceeding 35 years.

faqs.question: Is there any negative marking in the CBT written examination?
faqs.answer: Yes. There is a negative marking of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer in the online CBT exam for all posts, EXCEPT for Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS), which has no negative marking.

faqs.question: What is the selection process for Group A posts?
faqs.answer: Selection for Group A posts consists of a Computer-Based Test (CBT) for 70 marks, followed by an Interview for 30 marks.

faqs.question: What is the selection process for Group B and Group C posts?
faqs.answer: Selection is based entirely on the performance in the online CBT comprising 100 marks, followed by a qualifying Skill Test where applicable (e.g., LDC, Stenographer Grade-III, Driver, Hindi Assistant).

faqs.question: Where will the online CBT examination be conducted?
faqs.answer: CBT will be conducted at test centers located in New Delhi/Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, Mumbai, Hyderabad, and Guwahati.

faqs.question: What is the application fee for Group A, Group B, and Group C posts?
faqs.answer: For Group A: UR/OBC pay Rs. 2000/- (Rs. 500 processing + Rs. 1500 exam fee). Exempt categories pay Rs. 500/-. For Group B: UR/OBC pay Rs. 1500/- (Rs. 500 processing + Rs. 1000 exam fee). Exempt categories pay Rs. 500/-. For Group C: UR/OBC pay Rs. 1300/- (Rs. 500 processing + Rs. 800 exam fee). Exempt categories pay Rs. 500/-.

faqs.question: Which categories of candidates are exempted from paying the examination fee?
faqs.answer: Candidates belonging to SC, ST, PwBD, EWS, Ex-Servicemen, and all Female candidates are exempted from paying the examination fee. They only pay the processing fee of Rs. 500/-.

faqs.question: What are the typing skill test requirements for the Lower Division Clerk (LDC) post?
faqs.answer: A typing speed of 35 words per minute in English or 30 words per minute in Hindi on a computer is required. The test duration is 10 minutes.

faqs.question: What is the skill test scheme for the Stenographer Grade-III post?
faqs.answer: A shorthand dictation test at a speed of 80 words per minute for 10 minutes. The transcription time is 50 minutes for English and 65 minutes for Hindi on a computer.

faqs.question: What are the sub-categories under the Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS) post?
faqs.answer: Sub-categories include: (i) Messenger, (ii) Ward Boy, (iii) Female Attendant, (iv) Aya, (v) Lab Attendant, and (vi) Pharmacy Attendant.

faqs.question: What are the qualifications and age limits for the Pharmacist post?
faqs.answer: Age: Between 18 and 25 years. Qualification: 10+2 with Science, 2 years Diploma in Pharmacy from a recognized institution, and registration with Central/State Pharmacy Council.

faqs.question: How can candidates make changes to their application form?
faqs.answer: Candidates can use the Modification Window between 3rd August and 5th August 2026. A non-refundable modification fee of Rs. 300/- is charged per attempt.

faqs.question: Can candidates make changes to their basic registration details during the modification window?
faqs.answer: No. Information provided during Step I (User Account Creation) cannot be modified through the modification window. Only step II and step III details can be updated.

faqs.question: Are candidates required to submit hard copies of their applications to CCRUM?
faqs.answer: No. The application must be submitted online only. No documents or hard copies should be sent to CCRUM by post or mail.

faqs.question: What are the minimum qualifying cut-off percentages in the CBT?
faqs.answer: A minimum of 25% marks for PwBD candidates and 30% marks for all other categories (UR, OBC, SC, ST, EWS).

faqs.question: Is there any age relaxation for Central Government Civilian Employees?
faqs.answer: Yes, Central Government Civilian Employees with at least 3 years of continuous service are eligible for age relaxation up to 40 years (45 years for SC/ST candidates) for Group C posts.

faqs.question: What are the specific eligibility conditions for the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) category?
faqs.answer: Gross annual family income must be below Rs. 8 Lakhs. Candidates whose families own 5 acres of agricultural land, a residential flat of 1000 sq ft, a residential plot of 100 sq yards in notified municipalities, or 200 sq yards in other areas are excluded.

faqs.question: What happens if a candidate fails to pay the required fee during the modification window?
faqs.answer: If the candidate fails to remit the modification fee, the modification will not be considered, and only the originally submitted application data will be used.

faqs.question: Who is the recruiting organization and what is the advertisement number?
faqs.answer: BEML Limited (A Government of India Undertaking). The advertisement number is KP/S/12/2026, dated 08.07.2026.

faqs.question: What are the start and end dates for the online application?
faqs.answer: The online application portal is active from the notification release date (08.07.2026) and closes at 18:00 Hrs on 01.08.2026.

faqs.question: How many total vacancies have been announced?
faqs.answer: A total of 23 executive vacancies across various engineering and management levels have been announced.

faqs.question: What is the crucial date for determining the age, qualification, and experience limits?
faqs.answer: All eligibility criteria, including age, qualification, and experience, will be reckoned as on the last date of submission of applications, which is 01.08.2026.

faqs.question: What are the positions and grades offered in this recruitment?
faqs.answer: Positions range from Grade-II to Grade-X: Engineer (Gr-II), Assistant Manager (Gr-III), Manager (Gr-IV), Senior Manager (Gr-V), Assistant General Manager (Gr-VI), Deputy General Manager (Gr-VII), General Manager (Gr-VIII), Chief General Manager (Gr-IX), and Executive Director (Gr-X).

faqs.question: What are the pay scales for BEML Executive positions?
What is the application fee and who is exempted?
faqs.answer: General, OBC, and EWS candidates must pay a non-refundable fee of Rs. 500/- plus applicable taxes. SC, ST, and PwD candidates are completely exempted from paying any application fee.

faqs.question: What are the required qualifications for Position Code 101 (Head Futuristic Product Innovation and Incubation Centre)?
faqs.answer: Mandatory: Full-time, First Class Degree in Mechanical/Mechatronics/Electronics/EEE Engineering with M.Tech/MS in Design from a recognized University/Institution. Desirable: Project Management Certification.

faqs.question: What is the mandatory experience for Post Code 101?
faqs.answer: The candidate should have at least 25 years of professional experience for Executive Director (Grade X) or 21 years for Chief General Manager (Grade IX), with at least 5 years of cumulative post-qualification experience in the last 12 years at a senior level of Engineering Design and Research in an organization of repute. Additionally, they must have headed a versatile engineering team in a company with a turnover of above Rs. 1000 Crore.

faqs.question: Can candidates with engineering degrees in allied branches apply?
faqs.answer: Yes, candidates with engineering degrees from allied branches of Mechanical, Electrical, and Electronics can also apply for relevant positions, provided they possess the required post-qualification experience.

faqs.question: Is there any requirement regarding the class/division of the qualifying degree?
faqs.answer: Yes, candidates must possess a First Class degree (minimum 60% marks as an aggregate of all semesters/years). Qualifying marks are relaxable by 5% (to 55%) for SC/ST and PwD candidates.

faqs.question: What are the age limits for the different grades?
faqs.answer: Reckoned on 01.08.2026: Gr-II: 29 years | Gr-III: 30 years | Gr-IV: 34 years | Gr-V: 39 years | Gr-VI: 42 years | Gr-VII: 45 years | Gr-VIII: 48 years | Gr-IX: 57 years (58 years for Post 102) | Gr-X: 57 years.

faqs.question: What are the age relaxation benefits for reserved categories?
faqs.answer: SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation, OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) candidates get 3 years, and PwD candidates get 10 years (over and above SC/ST/OBC limits, subject to minimum 40% disability).

faqs.question: Is there any relaxation in age based on excess experience?
faqs.answer: Yes, the upper age limit can be relaxed for all categories subject to equivalent years of excess post-qualification experience. However, the maximum age with relaxation cannot exceed 57 years (58 years for Job Code 102).

faqs.question: Are private sector candidates eligible to apply for senior roles like GM, CGM, or ED?
faqs.answer: Yes, but private sector candidates applying for GM, CGM, or ED roles must be employed in a regular capacity in a company registered under the Companies Act with an annual turnover of Rs. 1000 Crore or more. Preference will be given to listed companies.

faqs.question: Is there a requirement to submit a No Objection Certificate (NOC)?
faqs.answer: Yes, candidates working in Government organizations, PSUs, or PSBs must submit a No Objection Certificate (NOC) specific to the applied position from their current employer at the time of interview.

faqs.question: What is the probation period for the recruited executives?
faqs.answer: The appointed candidates will be on probation for a period of one year from the date of joining, and further continuance/confirmation depends on performance and verification of credentials.

faqs.question: Where will selected candidates be posted?
faqs.answer: Selected candidates will be liable for posting at any place in India and abroad as per the requirements of BEML. Initial posting locations mentioned in the notification include Bengaluru, KGF, and Mysore.

faqs.question: What is the experience requirement for Post Code 111 (Senior Manager R&D - FEA/CAE)?
faqs.answer: A minimum of 11 years of post-qualification experience in Structural Simulation/Finite Element Analysis (FEA), with at least 10 years of hands-on experience using HyperMesh, ANSYS, Abaqus, Nastran, Opti-Struct, or LS-DYNA.

faqs.question: What is the mandatory qualification and experience for Post Code 118 (Raj Bhasha Official Language)?
faqs.answer: A Master's degree in Hindi/Hindi Translation with English at the Bachelor's level, or a Master's in English with Hindi at the Bachelor's level + PG Diploma in Translation, with a minimum of 4 years of post-qualification experience in Hindi/translation work.

faqs.question: What is the experience write-up requirement in the application form?
faqs.answer: Candidates are required to provide a detailed pen picture of at least 150 words for each experience claimed in the application form, clearly showing its relevance to the position applied for. Failure or vague descriptions will lead to rejection.

faqs.question: What are the eligibility criteria for Post Code 102 (Head Armoured Business)?
faqs.answer: The candidate must be a retired/serving Brigadier from the Indian Army with a Degree in Engineering from a recognized university/institution or equivalent. Knowledge of modern combat vehicles is mandatory.

faqs.question: Does BEML accept freelance experience as part of experience criteria?
faqs.answer: No, BEML will not consider freelance experience as part of Post Qualification Experience (PQE).

faqs.question: How must Government, PSU, or PSB employees submit their applications?
faqs.answer: They must apply online first, and then forward the printout of the online application through proper channel (or bring NOC at the time of interview) within 10 days from the closing date of the advertisement to the Sr. Manager (Recruitment Cell), BEML Soudha, Bengaluru.

faqs.question: Can candidates apply for more than one position?
faqs.answer: The official notification states that candidates shall apply for a single position which is most suitable.

overview: The Ministry of Railways, Government of India, through the Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs), has issued the Centralised Employment Notification (CEN) No. 02/2026 for the recruitment of Technician Grade-I Signal and various categories of Technician Grade-III.

The notification announces a grand total of 6557 vacancies across 25 different technician trades and disciplines. Of these, 323 vacancies are for Technician Grade-I Signal (Pay Level 5 under 7th CPC), and 6234 vacancies are for Technician Grade-III (Pay Level 2 under 7th CPC).

Eligible candidates with qualifications ranging from Matriculation/SSLC plus ITI (NCVT/SCVT), Course Completed Act Apprenticeship (CCAA), 10+2 with Physics and Mathematics, to B.Sc, Diploma, or Degree in Engineering can apply online. The selection will be conducted through a single-stage Computer Based Test (CBT) for each pay level, followed by Document Verification (DV) and medical fitness assessments.

topics: General Awareness: Knowledge of Current affairs, Indian geography, culture and history of India including freedom struggle, Indian Polity and constitution, Indian Economy, Environmental issues concerning India and the World, Sports, General scientific and technological developments, etc.

General Intelligence and Reasoning: Analogies, Alphabetical and Number Series, Coding and Decoding, Mathematical operations, Relationships, Syllogism, Jumbling, Venn Diagram, Data Interpretation and Sufficiency, Conclusions and decision making, Similarities and differences, Analytical reasoning, Classification, Directions, Statement – Arguments and Assumptions, etc.

Basics of Computers and Applications: Architecture of Computers; input and Output devices; Storage devices, Networking, Operating System like Windows, Unix, Linux; MS Office; Various data representation; Internet and Email; Websites & Web Browsers; Computer Virus.

Mathematics: Number system, Rational and irrational numbers, BODMAS rule, Quadratic Equations, Arithmetic Progression, Similar Triangles, Pythagoras Theorem, Co-ordinate Geometry, Trigonometrical Ratios, Heights and distances, Surface area and Volume; Sets: Sets and their representations, Empty set, Finite and Infinite sets, Equal sets, Subsets, Subsets of a set of real numbers, Universal set, Venn diagrams, Union and Intersection of sets, Difference of sets, Complement of a set, Properties of Complement; Statistics: Measures of Dispersion: Range, Mean deviation, variance and standard deviation of ungrouped/grouped data; probability occurrence of events, exhaustive events, mutually exclusive events.

Basic Science and Engineering: Physics fundamentals- Units, Measurements, Mass, Weight, Density, Work, Power, and Energy, Speed and Velocity, Heat and Temperature; Electricity and Magnetism- Electric Charge, Field, and Intensity, Electric Potential and Potential Difference, Simple Electric Circuits, Conductors, Non-conductors/Insulators, Ohm’s Law and its Limitations, Resistances in Series and Parallel of a Circuit and Specific Resistance, Relation between Electric Potential, Energy, and Power (Wattage), Ampere’s Law, Magnetic Force on Moving Charged Particle and Long Straight Conductors, Electromagnetic Induction, Faraday’s Law, and Electromagnetic Flux, Magnetic Field, Magnetic Induction; Electronics and Measurements- Basic Electronics, Digital Electronics, Electronic Devices and Circuits, Microcontroller, Microprocessor, Electronic Measurements, Measuring Systems and Principles, Range Extension Methods, Cathode Ray Oscilloscope, LCD, LED Panel, Transducers.

Mathematics: Number system, BODMAS, Decimals, Fractions, LCM, HCF, Ratio and Proportion, Percentages, Mensuration, Time and Work; Time and Distance, Simple and Compound Interest, Profit and Loss, Algebra, Geometry and Trigonometry, Elementary Statistics, Square Root, Age Calculations, Calendar & Clock, Pipes & Cistern etc.

General Intelligence and Reasoning: Analogies, Alphabetical and Number Series, Coding and Decoding, Mathematical operations, Relationships, Syllogism, Jumbling, Venn Diagram, Data Interpretation and Sufficiency, Conclusions and decision making, Similarities and differences, Analytical reasoning, Classification, Directions, Statement – Arguments and Assumptions etc.
General Science: The syllabus under this shall cover Physics, Chemistry and Life Sciences of 10th standard level.
General Awareness: On current affairs in science & technology, sports, culture, personalities, economics, politics and any other subject of importance.

reservation.title: Community, Vertical & Horizontal Reservation Guidelines:
detailsList: Vertical reservation exists for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and Other Backward Classes Non-Creamy Layer (OBC-NCL).
Horizontal reservation is provided for Ex-Servicemen (ExSM) and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) irrespective of their community.
OBC Non-Creamy Layer certificate in prescribed format (Annexure II) must be issued on or after April 01, 2026, and submitted along with a self-declaration (Annexure IIA) during document verification.

EWS Certificate: Family gross annual income must be below Rs. 8 Lakh for the financial year 2025-26 (prior to the application year 2026). Family assets must not exceed 5 acres of agricultural land, a 1000 sq ft residential flat, or specified plot sizes.

PwBD Reservation: Minimum 40% of relevant benchmark disability is required. Disability certificate must be issued by a competent medical authority in Annexure V(A) or V(B) as per Right of Persons with Disabilities Amendment Rules 2024.

examCentres.title: CBT Center Allocation & Rules:
examCentres.details: City allocation, centre allocation, and dates for CBT will be allotted based on technical and logistical feasibility. Candidates may have to travel to other cities or states for attending the CBT. Requests for a change of examination date, centre, shift, etc. shall not be allowed under any circumstances. E-call letters containing exact centre details will be made available for download 4 days prior to the examination.

howToApply: Step 1: Open the official career portal of participating RRBs or directly go to rrbapply.gov.in.

Step 2: Click on 'Create an Account' to register. Provide a valid mobile number and personal email ID. Fill in the name, father's name, mother's name, and Date of Birth exactly as recorded in your Matriculation/10th class certificate. (Details filled in the Create an Account form cannot be modified).
Step 3: Authenticate your identity using DigiLocker or Aadhaar. Aadhaar-seeded authentication facilitates smoother and faster verification at all stages of recruitment.

Step 4: Log in using your credentials and select the chosen RRB and relevant posts under the respective Pay Level (Level 5 or Level 2). Once submitted, the chosen RRB cannot be changed for that Pay Level.

Step 5: Fill in educational qualifications, community details, and previous experience if any. Candidates must ensure they fulfill all eligibility requirements on or before the closing date 29.07.2026.

Step 6: Capture a live photograph during the application process (no pre-existing photo upload is needed). Ensure to wear non-white, dark clothing and stand in front of a contrasting background without caps, masks, or spectacles.

Step 7: Upload a scanned copy of your signature written in running handwriting (cursive letters, not block/capital letters) using a black ink pen on white paper. Scanned file size must be between 30 KB and 49 KB (dimensions 140x60 pixels, minimum 100 DPI).
Step 8: Upload SC/ST certificate in PDF format (less than 400 KB) if requesting free train travel pass.
Step 9: Pay the non-refundable examination fee online through internet banking, debit/credit cards, or UPI. All service charges are to be borne by the candidate.

Step 10: Submit the order of post preferences for the chosen Zonal Railways/PUs, verify all entries, and complete the final submission. Take a printout of the submitted application form for record keeping.

faqs.question: What is the recruiting organization and what is the advertisement number?
faqs.answer: The recruitment is conducted by the Ministry of Railways, Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs). The centralized advertisement number is CEN No. 02/2026.

faqs.question: What are the start and end dates for submission of online applications?
faqs.answer: The online application portal opens on 30.06.2026 and closes at 23:59 Hrs on 29.07.2026.

faqs.question: How many total vacancies have been announced in CEN 02/2026?
faqs.answer: A grand total of 6557 vacancies have been announced, consisting of 323 vacancies for Technician Grade-I Signal and 6234 vacancies for various Technician Grade-III posts.

faqs.question: What is the crucial date for determining age, qualification, and community status?
faqs.answer: All eligibility criteria, including educational/technical qualifications, age limit, and reservation claims, will be reckoned as on the closing date of application submission, which is 29.07.2026.

faqs.question: What are the pay levels and initial pay scales for the notified posts?
faqs.answer: Technician Grade-I Signal is in Pay Level 5 with an initial pay of Rs. 29,200/- per month. Technician Grade-III is in Pay Level 2 with an initial pay of Rs. 19,900/- per month.

faqs.question: What is the age limit for Technician Grade-I Signal and Grade-III?
faqs.answer: As on 01.07.2026, the age limit is 18 to 33 years for Technician Grade-I Signal and 18 to 30 years for Technician Grade-III.

faqs.question: What are the age relaxation benefits for SC/ST and OBC candidates?
faqs.answer: SC and ST candidates receive an age relaxation of 5 years. OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) candidates receive an age relaxation of 3 years in the upper age limit.

faqs.question: Are candidates awaiting their final exam results eligible to apply?
faqs.answer: No. Candidates must possess and fulfill all the prescribed educational and technical qualifications on or before the closing date (29.07.2026). Those waiting for final results are not eligible and should not apply.

faqs.question: Is a Diploma or Degree in Engineering accepted in lieu of ITI for Technician Grade-III posts?
faqs.answer: No. For Technician Grade-III posts (Pay Level 2), a Diploma or Degree in Engineering will NOT be accepted in lieu of Course Completed Act Apprenticeship (CCAA) or ITI, unless otherwise specified in the official post parameters.

faqs.question: What is the qualification required for Technician Grade-I Signal?
faqs.answer: Candidates must possess a Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.) in Physics/Electronics/Computer Science/IT/Instrumentation OR a combination of any of these sub-streams; OR a 3-year Diploma in Engineering in these basic streams; OR a 4-year Degree in Engineering in these basic streams from a recognized University/Institution.

faqs.question: What is the qualification required for Technician Grade-III S&T (Category 14)?
faqs.answer: Candidates must possess Matriculation/SSLC plus ITI in Electrician / Electronics Mechanic / Wireman; OR Matriculation/SSLC plus CCAA in the same trades; OR 10+2 with Physics and Mathematics from a recognized board.

faqs.question: What is the application fee for general and reserved categories?
faqs.answer: General, OBC, and EWS candidates must pay a fee of Rs. 500/-, of which Rs. 400/- is refundable on appearing in CBT. SC, ST, Ex-Servicemen, PwBD, Female, Transgender, Minorities, and EBC candidates pay Rs. 250/-, which is fully refundable (Rs. 250/-) on appearing in CBT.

faqs.question: Are candidates who do not appear in the CBT eligible for a fee refund?
faqs.answer: No. Only candidates who actually attend the Computer Based Test (CBT) will receive a refund of their examination fee as applicable. Absent candidates forfeit their fee.

faqs.question: How is the examination fee refund credited?
faqs.answer: The refund (duly deducting bank charges as applicable) is credited only to the bank account seeded with the candidate's Aadhaar number, which is verified during the registration process.

faqs.question: Who is considered an Economically Backward Class (EBC) candidate for fee concession?
faqs.answer: EBC candidates are those whose annual family income is less than Rs. 50,000/-. They must hold a valid Income Certificate in prescribed format (Annexure IIIA), a BPL Card, or an Izzat MST at the time of filling up the application.

faqs.question: Is an EBC candidate entitled to job reservation?
faqs.answer: No. An Economically Backward Class (EBC) candidate is entitled only to a concessional examination fee and is NOT entitled to job reservation.

faqs.question: Can a candidate apply for more than one RRB or submit multiple applications?
faqs.answer: No. A candidate must choose only one RRB for a given Pay Level and submit only one common online application. Submitting multiple applications or applying to more than one RRB for the same Pay Level will result in summary rejection of all applications and debarment.

faqs.question: What is the selection process for RRB Technicians?
faqs.answer: The recruitment process comprises three stages: (i) Computer Based Test (CBT), (ii) Document Verification (DV) based on CBT merit, and (iii) Medical Examination (ME).

faqs.question: Is there any negative marking in the Computer Based Test (CBT)?
faqs.answer: Yes, there is negative marking in the CBT. One-third (1/3rd) of the marks allotted for a question will be deducted for each wrong answer.

faqs.question: What is the exam pattern and duration for Technician Grade-I Signal?
faqs.answer: The CBT has a duration of 90 minutes with 100 multiple-choice questions. Marks distribution: General Awareness (10), General Intelligence and Reasoning (15), Basics of Computers and Applications (20), Mathematics (20), and Basic Science and Engineering (35).

faqs.question: What is the exam pattern and duration for Technician Grade-III posts?
faqs.answer: The CBT has a duration of 90 minutes with 100 multiple-choice questions. Marks distribution: Mathematics (25), General Intelligence & Reasoning (25), General Science (40), and General Awareness (10).

faqs.question: Are candidates who have undergone LASIK surgery eligible for Track Machine posts?
faqs.answer: No. Technician Grade III Track Machine posts require Medical Standard A3. Candidates who have undergone LASIK surgery or any other surgical procedure to correct refractory errors are NOT eligible for posts requiring A3 standard.

faqs.question: How can SC/ST candidates avail of the free train travel facility?
faqs.answer: Eligible SC and ST candidates who opt for the free train travel pass in their online application will receive the free sleeper class railway pass printed directly on their e-call letter. They must carry their original caste certificate during the journey.

faqs.question: Can details in the 'Create an Account' form or the 'Chosen RRB' be modified later?
faqs.answer: No. Details filled in the 'Create an Account' form (including mobile number and Email ID) and the chosen RRB for a pay level cannot be modified or changed at any stage under any circumstances.

faqs.question: What is the fee for modifying other details in the online application?
faqs.answer: Candidates can modify other details (excluding Create an Account details and Chosen RRB) during the modification window (01.08.2026 to 10.08.2026) by paying a non-refundable modification fee of Rs. 250/- per occasion.

faqs.question: What are the required specifications for uploading the signature?
faqs.answer: The signature must be written by the candidate in running handwriting (cursive letters, not block/capital letters) using a black ink pen on white paper, scanned at minimum 100 DPI, and uploaded in JPG/JPEG format with file size between 30 KB and 49 KB.

faqs.question: Do candidates need to upload a pre-existing photograph?
faqs.answer: No. Pre-existing photograph upload is not allowed. The application module is designed to capture a live photograph of the candidate during the online application process. Candidates must wear non-white dark clothing.

faqs.question: How is Scribe registration handled?
faqs.answer: Any person who wishes to offer services as a scribe must register themselves using their account credentials on the RRB portal rrbapply.gov.in to generate a scribe OTR number. Candidates must log in and enter this OTR number during the scribe window (11.08.2026 to 15.08.2026).

faqs.question: Are Government or PSU employees required to submit an NOC?
faqs.answer: Yes. Candidates serving in any Central/State Government Department, including Railways or PSUs, must produce an official No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their employer on the date of Document Verification, failing which their candidature will be cancelled.

overview: Northeast Frontier Railway (NFR), Personnel Department, Maligaon (Guwahati), has released a centralized notification (No. NFR/NAPS/ACT APP./2026) dated 14-07-2026 for the engagement of Act Apprentices.

The recruitment seeks to engage eligible candidates against 6777 slots for imparting training under the Apprentices Act 1961 in various designated trades across Workshops, Divisions, and Units of NFR for the training slots of years 2025-2026 & 2026-2027.

Interested and eligible candidates who possess 10th/12th qualification with ITI in respective trades from recognized institutions can apply online. The selection is strictly based on the academic merit (average of Matriculation and ITI marks) and successful document verification. No written examination or interview will be conducted.

Crucial Qualification Clause: Candidates must have already completed and possessed the prescribed certificates/NTC/STC as on the date of this notification. Candidates awaiting final results are strictly NOT eligible.

Shortlisted candidates up to 1.5 times the number of notified slots will be called for verification of original testimonials, qualification certificates, caste status, and age proofs at the respective division or unit.

Preparation for Document Verification: Candidates must prepare all original certificates, marks sheets of Class 10 and ITI semesters, Caste certificates (Annexure IX/X), EWS certificate (Annexure XII), PwBD certificate (Annexure XIII/XIV/XV), and Medical fitness certificate (Annexure XI).

reservation.title: Community and Horizontal Reservation Guidelines:
detailsList: Vertical reservations are applicable for SC, ST, OBC (Non-Creamy Layer), and EWS categories as per the extant rules.
EWS Reservation: 10% vertical reservation. Candidates must upload an Income & Asset Certificate issued on or after 01.04.2026 in the prescribed format (Annexure-XII).
Horizontal Reservation: 10% slots are reserved for Ex-Servicemen (ExSM) and 4% slots for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD).

OBC (NCL) candidates must submit a valid Caste Certificate as per Annexure-X, and SC/ST candidates must submit a Caste Certificate as per Annexure-IX, issued by authorized authorities like District Magistrate, Revenue Officer (Tahsildar), or Sub-divisional Officer.

If suitable SC candidates are not available, the remaining slots will be filled by ST candidates, and vice-versa. If suitable candidates are still not available, the unfilled SC/ST/OBC/EWS slots will be filled by UR candidates.

No travel expenses or daily allowances are admissible for attending DV.

howToApply: Step 1: Visit the official website of Northeast Frontier Railway (www.nfr.indianrailways.gov.in).
Step 2: Navigate to General Info --> Departments --> Personnel --> Act Apprentice Notification, and click on the online application link.
Step 3: Register as a new user by providing basic details such as Name, DOB, active mobile number, and personal email ID. Fill in the training unit preference order carefully.

Step 4: Log in using the system-generated credentials and fill out the academic details (Matriculation and ITI marks, or 12th science marks as applicable). Candidates are allowed to submit only one application.
Step 5: Upload high-quality legible scanned copies of mandatory documents (Matric marksheet/certificate, ITI semesters marksheet, NCVT/SCVT Trade certificate, proof of DOB, Caste certificate, etc.).
Step 6: Upload a scanned copy of your color photograph (with front view, no cap/sunglasses) and signature as per specifications.
Step 7: Pay the non-refundable application fee of Rs. 100/- online using the integrated payment gateway (SC, ST, PwBD, EBC, and Women candidates are exempted).
Step 8: Verify all entries, submit the application form, and take a printout of the final submitted application form for future record.

importantInstructions: RED ALERT: Candidates who do not possess the completed qualification certificates or are awaiting final results as on the date of this notification (14-07-2026) are strictly NOT eligible to apply.
RED ALERT: Submission of multiple applications or trying to apply to more than one unit/division will lead to summary rejection of all applications and candidate disqualification.
RED ALERT: Providing false or wrong declarations of academic/ITI marks in the online form will result in immediate disqualification and possible debarment from future Railway recruitments.
YELLOW WARNING: Once the application is submitted, no modification to registration details is allowed. Candidates can modify other online details on payment of Rs. 50/- per occasion.

YELLOW WARNING: No hostel accommodation or lodging arrangements will be provided by NFR. Selected apprentices must make their own boarding and lodging arrangements for the entire 1-year training period.

faqs.question: What is the recruiting organization and the notification number for this vacancy?
faqs.answer: The recruitment is conducted by the Northeast Frontier Railway (NFR), Personnel Department, Maligaon, Guwahati. The advertisement number is Notification No. NFR/NAPS/ACT APP./2026 dated 14-07-2026.

faqs.question: What are the start and end dates for submitting online applications?
faqs.answer: The online application window opens on 20-07-2026 at 09:00 hrs and closes on 19-08-2026 at 17:30 hrs.

faqs.question: How many total vacancies/slots are available for NFR Act Apprentice 2026?
faqs.answer: A grand total of 6777 training slots are available across various Divisions, Workshops, and Units under NFR.

faqs.question: What is the selection process for the NFR Act Apprentice engagement?
faqs.answer: The selection is 100% merit-based. There is no written examination, online test, or interview. Selection is made based on the average percentage of marks obtained in Matriculation (min 50% aggregate) and the ITI trade marks.

faqs.question: How is the final merit list calculated for selection?
faqs.answer: The final merit list is prepared on the average of percentage marks obtained in Matriculation (Class 10) and ITI trade exams (50% weightage each). For Medical Lab Technicians, it is calculated based on Matriculation (min 50%) and 12th Science (PCB) marks.

faqs.question: What is the age limit for NFR Act Apprentice 2026?
faqs.answer: As on the closing date (19-08-2026), candidates must be at least 15 years old and must not have completed 24 years of age.

faqs.question: Are there any upper age relaxations for reserved categories?
faqs.answer: Yes, upper age relaxation is provided as follows: 5 years for SC/ST candidates, 3 years for OBC-NCL candidates, 10 years for PwBD candidates, and 10 additional years (plus defense service period) for Ex-Servicemen.

faqs.question: Can candidates who are waiting for their final ITI results apply?
faqs.answer: No. Candidates must possess the prescribed qualifications and be in possession of their ITI pass certificate/NTC/STC as on the date of the notification (14-07-2026). Awaiting result candidates are not eligible.

faqs.question: Is a Diploma or Degree in Engineering acceptable in lieu of ITI for these posts?
faqs.answer: No. A Diploma or Degree in Engineering is not acceptable in lieu of ITI, as the minimum required qualification for these slots is Matriculation plus ITI (NCVT/SCVT) in the notified trades.

faqs.question: What are the eligibility criteria for Medical Laboratory Technician posts?
faqs.answer: Candidates must have passed the 12th class examination under the 10+2 system with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology, securing a minimum of 50% aggregate marks in both 10th and 12th standard examinations. ITI is not required for these posts.

faqs.question: What is the application fee for NFR Act Apprentice 2026?
faqs.answer: The non-refundable application fee is Rs. 100/-. SC, ST, PwBD, EBC, and Women candidates are completely exempted from paying any application fee.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to claim the fee exemption as an EBC candidate?
faqs.answer: EBC (Economically Backward Class) candidates are those whose annual family income is less than Rs. 50,000/-. They must hold and upload a valid Income Certificate as per Annexure-XVI, issued on or after 01-04-2026.

faqs.question: Can I apply for multiple training units or divisions?
faqs.answer: No. A candidate can submit only ONE application in total. Candidates must thoroughly read the training slots and indicate their choice of Units in order of preference clearly in their online form.

faqs.question: What is the monthly stipend paid during the NFR apprenticeship training?
faqs.answer: The minimum stipend is Rs. 9,600/- per month for NTC/STC holders (w.e.f. 11.09.2025). For courses where 1 or 2 years’ exemption is admissible under the curriculum, the stipend is Rs. 10,560/- (2nd year) and Rs. 11,040/- (3rd year) respectively.

faqs.question: Does NFR provide hostel accommodation or daily allowances during training?
faqs.answer: No hostel accommodation or daily/travel allowances are provided during training or for document verification. Selected candidates must make their own boarding & lodging arrangements.

faqs.question: Does completing this apprenticeship training guarantee a permanent job in Railways?
faqs.answer: No. Imparting of training under the Apprentice Act 1961 does not confer any automatic right or claim for regular appointment or absorption in railway services.

faqs.question: What benefit do Course Completed Act Apprentices (CCAA) get in regular railway recruitments?
faqs.answer: Selected CCAAs possessing National Apprenticeship Certificates (NAC) will receive a 20% preference in vacancies notified for erstwhile Group D (Level-1) posts in Zonal Railways.

faqs.question: What medical standards must candidates fulfill, and what medical certificate is required?
faqs.answer: Candidates must meet the prescribed physical and medical standards and submit a Medical Certificate as per Annexure-XI signed by a Government authorized Gazetted Doctor, not below the rank of Assistant Surgeon of a Central/State Hospital.

faqs.question: What are the training slots allocated for Katihar (KIR) Division?
faqs.answer: Katihar (KIR) & Tindharia (TDH) Workshop is allocated a total of 1103 slots across various departments and trades.

faqs.question: Is there a modification fee for correcting application details after submission?
faqs.answer: Yes. Candidates can make corrections in their online application form after submission on payment of Rs. 50/- for each occasion. Registration details cannot be modified.

faqs.question: What happens if two or more candidates secure the same average percentage marks?
faqs.answer: In case of equal marks, the older candidate in age will be ranked higher. If the date of birth is also identical, the candidate who passed the matriculation exam earlier will be preferred.

faqs.question: What is the ratio of candidates called for Document Verification?
faqs.answer: Shortlisted candidates will be called for Document Verification to the extent of 1.5 times the number of notified slots.

faqs.question: What certificates must be produced in original during Document Verification?
faqs.answer: Candidates must bring original Matric marksheet & pass certificate, Class 12 marksheet (for Med Lab Tech), Consolidated ITI marksheet or NTC/Provisional Trade Certificate, Caste/EWS/PwBD certificates, and a completed Medical fitness certificate (Annexure XI).

faqs.question: Are candidates from states outside Assam, West Bengal, and Bihar eligible to apply?
faqs.answer: Yes, eligible candidates from all states in India can apply, provided they meet the academic qualifications, age limits, and other specified conditions in the notification.

faqs.question: What is the priority order for engaging children of Ex-Servicemen (ExSM)?
faqs.answer: Priority: (a) Children of deceased/disabled ExSM including those killed/disabled during peace time, (b) Children of ExSM, (c) Children of serving Jawans, (d) Children of serving officers, (e) Ex-Servicemen.

faqs.answer: The post is in Pay Level 10 with a Basic Pay scale of Rs. 56,100 – 1,77,500. The initial CTC is approximately Rs. 15.68 Lakhs per annum.

faqs.question: What components are included in the ICAI salary package?
faqs.answer: The compensation consists of Basic Pay, Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance, National Pension System (NPS), Ex. Gratia for academic pursuit, LTC, and Gratuity.

faqs.question: What is the application fee for this recruitment and is it refundable?
faqs.answer: The application fee is Rs. 500/- (inclusive of all taxes) and is strictly non-refundable.

faqs.question: Can I apply via offline mode, post, or email?
faqs.answer: No. Only online applications will be accepted. Applications sent via post, hand, email, or other modes will be rejected.

faqs.question: Should I send a hard copy of my application or CV to the ICAI office?
faqs.answer: No, candidates are requested not to send hard copies or CVs to the Institute. Original documents must be brought at the time of the Interview.

faqs.question: What is the exam pattern and duration for the CBT?
faqs.answer: The Computer Based Test (CBT) duration is 150 minutes, carrying a total of 150 marks. It includes MCQ and descriptive questions in English.

faqs.question: What is the structure of sections in the CBT?
faqs.answer: The exam has two main sections: (1) General Section: Part A MCQ (30 questions, 30 marks) and Part B Descriptive (2 questions, 30 marks), and (2) Technical Section MCQ (90 questions, 90 marks).

faqs.question: Is there a penalty for wrong answers in the written exam?
faqs.answer: Yes, a negative marking of 0.25 marks is applicable for each wrong MCQ answer. There is no negative marking for descriptive questions.

faqs.question: What is the syllabus for the Technical Section of the exam?
faqs.answer: The syllabus includes: Accounting Standards, Advanced Auditing, Assurance & Professional Ethics, Financial Reporting, Corporate and Other Laws, Financial Management & Strategic Management, Direct Tax Laws & International Taxation, Indirect Tax Laws, and Information Systems.

faqs.question: Are outstation candidates paid any travel allowance for attending the interview?
faqs.answer: Yes. Outstation candidates will be reimbursed travel expenses by the shortest route as per rules of the ICAI.

faqs.question: What is the probation period for selected Executive Officers?
faqs.answer: Selected candidates will be placed on probation for a period of one year, which may be extended based on non-satisfactory performance.

faqs.question: Are current government employees required to submit any certificates?
faqs.answer: Yes, candidates serving in Central/State Government, Public Sector Enterprises, or Autonomous bodies must mandatorily produce a "No Objection Certificate" (NOC) at the time of the Interview.

syllabus.section: Job Description - Finance Officer (Grade II) & Deputy Manager (Grade III)
topics: Preparation and finalization of Annual Accounts, working knowledge on preparations of Accounts.
Knowledge of Receivables and Debtors Management.
Knowledge of Costing Systems and Cost accounting.
Knowledge of Accounting Standards & Cost Accounting Standards.
Interaction with Statutory Auditors & Internal Auditors.
Cash Management & dealing with Banks and Financial Institutions.
Knowledge of Direct and Indirect Taxes.
Sound conceptual and analytical ability.
Functional knowledge of ERP & hands on experience of working on computers.
Core knowledge of Accounting.
Experience in 3-D Modelling, Assembly, Kinematics, Tolerance analysis, drawings and GD&T.
Background in Machine Design, Mechanics of Materials, Dynamics and Vibration, Finite Element Analysis.
Experience with CAD software (e.g., CATIA, UG) and PLM tools like Teamcentre, Enovia.
Experience in using Multibody Dynamics simulation using tools like MSC ADAMS, SIMULINK, MATLAB, Amesim.
Experience preferably in Aerospace industry with knowledge of regulatory requirements like MIL, FAR standards.
Familiarity with manufacturing process and design for manufacturing and assembly (DFMA).
Experience in preparation of detailed design documentation, reports, and presentations.
Design of Avionics Architecture for meeting customer requirements.
Design of wiring logics/schematic/drawing, Loom drawings and associated documents required for Avionics operation.
Prepare documents for Avionics/Electronics Systems design and technical documentation.
Experience in Electronics/Avionics Systems Design or Installation, platform integration, and flight testing at HAL & Customer sites.
Knowledge of Avionics digital data bus protocol, bus load analysis for aircraft interface.
Knowledge on development of FHA and SSA for Avionics systems integration on helicopters.
Basic knowledge of using avionics test equipment (protocol & bus analyzers, data acquisition systems, flight test instrumentation) and failure debugging.
Coordinate procurement activities: Market surveys, vendor identification, technical evaluation, design reviews (PDR, CDR) & certification.

Understanding of Basic Navigation/Communication System/Antenna Systems of Aircraft or equivalent, Environmental Qualification testing, EMI/EMC, and military/civil standards (MIL-STD-810, MIL-STD-461, MIL-STD-464, DO 160, DO-178, DO-254, FAR).
Design of Electrical Architecture for meeting customer requirements.
Design of Electrical wiring logics/wiring diagrams required for operation of aircraft systems.
Design and development of detailed electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and interconnection diagrams for simulator components.
Electrical load analysis and design of electrical power distribution systems from UPS or Main incomer to simulator systems.
Prepare documents for Electrical System design and technical specification with wiring schematics and loom drawings.
Minimize Electro Magnetic Interference (EMI) and ensure Electro Magnetic Compatibility (EMC).
Usage of Oscilloscopes, Programmable Power Supplies, Clamp Meters, Earth Resistance Meters and Multimeters to diagnose hardware issues.
Market surveys, vendor identification, obtaining budgetary quotations, and preparing RFPs as per customer requirements.
Preparation of Preliminary Design Review (PDR) and Critical Design Review (CDR) documents.
Installation, Integration, and testing of Electrical systems at HAL and Customer sites.
Preparation of Bill of Materials (BoM), discussion with vendors, study of related design/analysis tools.

syllabus: Post Code 01 (Bioinstrumentation / Biophysics / Medical Physics): Design & validation of wearable health monitoring sensors and systems & biomedical sensor instrumentation; bio-signal data acquisition & processing (ECG, EEG, EMG), noise reduction & feature extraction; medical imaging and informatics; development of portable diagnostic devices and wearable sensors.

Post Code 02 (Developmental Biology / Biotechnology): Radiation biology & exposure models; regenerative approaches to preserve musculoskeletal integrity during spaceflight; mammalian and stem cell culture, primary cell lines, 3D/organoid culture systems; in vivo and ex vivo animal physiological studies; astronaut disease biology models; host-pathogen interaction studies under stress and microgravity.

Post Code 03 (Cellular & Molecular Biology / Cell Biology): Immune and cellular adaptation across astronaut health cycle; bioinformatics analysis of proteomic data for biomarker identification; molecular cloning, confocal microscopy, live-cell imaging, gene editing; large-scale proteomic dataset analysis, gene expression & statistical workflows.

Post Code 04 (Computational Biology / Systems Biology / Bioinformatics): In-silico models to anticipate astronaut adaptation, assess countermeasures & guide rehabilitation; development of therapeutics and space-grade diagnostics; multi-omics integration for spaceflight stressors; modeling cellular pathways, host-microbe interactions & metabolic networks; computational simulation of closed-loop life support systems; generative models & Digital Twin Biology using neural networks and deep learning.

Post Code 05 (Biomedical Engineering / Biomechanics): Gait analysis, exercise countermeasure, motion capture & force-plate studies, rehabilitation program development; biomechanical analysis of musculoskeletal system; human performance data analysis from wearables; rodent/human analog design for spaceflight experiments.

Post Code 06 (Biomedical Engineering / Bio-imaging & DSP): Development & validation of bio-imaging systems for microgravity tissue changes (strictly confidential); implementation of DSP algorithms for ECG/EEG/EMG from wearables; bioinformatics dataset analysis for space radiation effects; portable diagnostic devices, biosensors, point-of-care testing & real-time astronaut health monitoring; biomedical device & lab-on-chip integration; AI/ML integration for real-time signal/imaging analysis.

faqs.question: Can GNM freshers apply for GIMS Staff Nurse Recruitment 2026?
faqs.answer: No. GNM freshers without the required experience are not eligible for this recruitment. For candidates applying through the GNM qualification, the notification requires: GNM/Diploma in General Nursing Midwifery from a recognized institute, registration with State or Indian Nursing Council, AND 2 years of experience after acquiring the qualification in a minimum 50-bedded hospital. Candidates with B.Sc Nursing or B.Sc Nursing (Post Basic) can apply as freshers provided they have valid nursing registration.

faqs.question: Is work experience required for GNM candidates?
faqs.answer: Yes. GNM candidates must have 2 years of experience after acquiring the GNM qualification in a minimum 50-bedded hospital. The experience must be obtained after acquiring the qualification and supported by proper documentary proof. B.Sc Nursing candidates do not require hospital experience.

faqs.question: Can candidates registered with Nursing Councils outside Uttar Pradesh apply?
faqs.answer: Yes. Candidates registered with a State Nursing Council outside Uttar Pradesh or the Indian Nursing Council can apply, provided they meet the other eligibility requirements. However, regarding reservation, only permanent residents/domiciles of Uttar Pradesh are eligible for SC/ST/OBC/EWS reserved posts. Other-state candidates will be considered under the Unreserved (UR) category.

faqs.question: Are Chhattisgarh state students eligible for GIMS Staff Nurse Recruitment 2026?
faqs.answer: Yes, candidates from Chhattisgarh (and all other Indian states) can apply if they satisfy the prescribed eligibility conditions (B.Sc Nursing or GNM with 2 yrs experience + Registration + Age). However, Chhattisgarh domicile candidates cannot claim UP reservation benefits and will be treated as Unreserved (UR) candidates.

faqs.question: Why is the GIMS Staff Nurse notification/link not showing on the official website?
faqs.answer: The notification has been officially released. The advertisement (Advt. No. GIMS/2026/Manpower/NT-03/10) is dated 09 August 2026, and online applications started on 10 August 2026. The application window is open until 07 September 2026 for 100 Staff Nurse (Non-Teaching) posts on the official GIMS website www.gims.ac.in.

faqs.question: Why is the GIMS Staff Nurse vacancy not listed on Sarkari Result?
faqs.answer: A vacancy does not need to appear on Sarkari Result or third-party websites to be official. The official GIMS website (www.gims.ac.in) is the final authority. The notification has been released and online applications are active. Candidates should verify details directly from the official GIMS website.

faqs.question: Where can I get the direct application link for GIMS Staff Nurse?
faqs.answer: The online application is available through the official GIMS recruitment portal at www.gims.ac.in. Candidates should complete registration, fill details, upload photo/signature/documents, pay the fee, and submit the form online between 10 August 2026 and 07 September 2026.

faqs.question: Can you make a detailed video on the full notification once available?
faqs.answer: The notification is already available covering all 16 key points: 100 vacancies, B.Sc Nursing vs GNM eligibility, GNM 2-year 50-bed hospital experience, Nursing Council registration, age limit (21-40 yrs), category-wise reservation, UP domicile rules, application fee (UR/OBC ₹1298, SC/ST ₹944), CBT exam pattern (100 MCQs), syllabus, 0.25 negative marking, exam cities, and selection process.

faqs.question: What is the overall age limit for GIMS Staff Nurse Recruitment 2026?
faqs.answer: The general age limit is Minimum 21 years and Maximum 40 years as on 01 July 2026. Candidates must be at least 21 years old and not older than 40 years on the cutoff date, subject to category-wise age relaxations.

faqs.question: What is the age limit and relaxation for the OBC category?
faqs.answer: Eligible OBC candidates of Uttar Pradesh receive up to 5 years of age relaxation (maximum age 45 years). However, this relaxation applies strictly to permanent residents/domiciles of UP. OBC candidates from other states will be treated as Unreserved (UR) candidates and must fall within the 40-year limit.

faqs.question: Is the upper age limit 40 years?
faqs.answer: Yes, the general upper age limit is 40 years as on 1 July 2026. Age relaxations include: UP SC/ST/OBC (up to 5 years), UP Govt employees (up to 5 years), Persons with Disabilities (15 years), and Ex-Servicemen (up to 3 years after deducting service).

faqs.question: What is the complete GIMS Staff Nurse exam syllabus & pattern?
faqs.answer: The CBT consists of 100 MCQs for 100 marks (Duration: 2 hours). Section A (60 Questions) covers Core Nursing; Section B (25 Questions) covers Applied Sciences & Protocols; Section C (15 Questions) covers Basic Sciences, English, and Community Health. 80% questions test theoretical knowledge and 20% test practical knowledge. Negative marking is 0.25 mark per wrong answer. Qualifying marks: UR/EWS/OBC 40%, SC/ST 35%.

faqs.question: Where will the GIMS Staff Nurse exam centres be located?
faqs.answer: The CBT examination will be conducted in Delhi/NCR, Lucknow, Gorakhpur, and Varanasi. Candidates can indicate city preferences during application, though final allocation depends on slot availability as indicated on the Admit Card.

faqs.question: What is the GIMS Staff Nurse application/examination fee?
faqs.answer: The application fee (including 18% GST) is: UR / OBC / EWS: ₹1,298 (₹1100 + ₹198 GST); SC / ST (UP Domicile): ₹944 (₹800 + ₹144 GST); Divyang (PwD UP Domicile): Exempted (Nil). Fee is non-refundable.

faqs.question: Is a caste certificate essential to attach/upload?
faqs.answer: Yes, if claiming SC/ST/OBC/EWS reservation benefits. Only permanent residents/domiciles of Uttar Pradesh are eligible for reservation. OBC/EWS certificates must be issued on or after 01 April 2026. Candidates from other states claiming reserved categories will be treated as General/UR.

faqs.question: When will the CRPF Nursing application start?
faqs.answer: CRPF Nursing recruitment is completely separate from GIMS Staff Nurse Recruitment. Candidates should not confuse GIMS with CRPF. GIMS Staff Nurse applications are open from 10 August to 07 September 2026 on www.gims.ac.in.

faqs.question: Where can we find full notification details for ESIC GNM?
faqs.answer: ESIC recruitment is separate from GIMS Staff Nurse recruitment. ESIC vacancies should be checked on www.esic.gov.in. Eligibility rules, hospital experience, and application dates vary between organizations.

faqs.question: Is anyone travelling to Delhi (NCR) for NORCET 11 preparation?
faqs.answer: NORCET 11 (conducted by AIIMS) and GIMS Staff Nurse 2026 are separate exams, though syllabus topics (Fundamentals, MS Nursing, Pediatrics, Obstetrics, Pharmacology) overlap significantly. Preparing for GIMS CBT also aids in NORCET preparation.

faqs.question: How are seats allocated across reserved vs general categories?
faqs.answer: Out of 100 total vacancies: UR: 40, OBC: 27, SC: 21, EWS: 10, ST: 2. Horizontal reservation applies for Women (20%), Ex-Servicemen (5%), PwD (4%), and DFF (2%). Non-UP candidates compete under 40 UR seats.

faqs.question: Is there any update on government hospital job openings vs private job options?
faqs.answer: GIMS Staff Nurse Recruitment 2026 is a permanent government sector recruitment for 100 regular Staff Nurse posts under UP Govt. B.Sc Nursing candidates and GNM candidates with 2 years 50-bed hospital experience are encouraged to apply before 07 September 2026.

faqs.question: Why are there 0 vacancies in Bihar, Jharkhand, Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Uttarakhand, etc. in SBI Clerk 2026?
faqs.answer: Because the 1,538 vacancies in this particular notification are backlog vacancies, not the new regular vacancies for the 2026–27 recruitment cycle. A backlog vacancy generally represents a reserved-category vacancy from an earlier recruitment that remained unfilled. Therefore, the distribution is completely different from what you would expect from a normal SBI Clerk notification. Zero in Delhi/Bihar/Haryana etc. does NOT mean SBI will have zero regular Clerk vacancies there this year.

faqs.question: Will SBI Clerk 2026 vacancies be updated or increased later?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but don't assume they will be. The current notification is specifically for the backlog drive. The much more important development for most aspirants will be the separate regular SBI Clerk notification, which should contain fresh state-wise vacancies for the new recruitment cycle. If your state has zero seats in the present notification, wait for the regular notification rather than concluding that SBI Clerk has no vacancy in your state.

faqs.question: Why is there no vacancy in Delhi, Haryana, and NCR for SBI Clerk 2026?
faqs.answer: This is a consequence of the backlog-vacancy nature of the current recruitment. It does not mean SBI has stopped recruiting Junior Associates in Delhi/NCR or Haryana. Also remember that SBI recruitment is organized according to State/UT/circle-wise vacancies, rather than simply according to where candidates live.

faqs.question: What should candidates from zero-vacancy states do for SBI Clerk 2026?
faqs.answer: Wait for the regular notification. If you're from Delhi, Haryana, Bihar, Jharkhand, Punjab, Uttarakhand, etc., choosing another state merely because it has backlog vacancies is not recommended unless you genuinely satisfy that state's local-language requirement and are eligible for the applicable reserved category. The regular notification is likely to be far more relevant.

faqs.question: Can I apply for SBI Clerk 2026 from another state?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to the notification's conditions — but the important issue is the local language. SBI's Junior Associate recruitment is state/UT based. Candidates apply for vacancies of one State/UT only and must qualify the specified local-language test (LPT) where applicable. For example, living in Delhi does not prevent you from applying for Maharashtra, but if you select Maharashtra, you must be prepared for Marathi language requirements.

faqs.question: How strict is the Language Proficiency Test (LPT) in SBI Clerk recruitment?
faqs.answer: It is a mandatory qualifying requirement. The LPT checks whether you know the specified local language of the selected state (e.g., Marathi for Maharashtra, Gujarati for Gujarat, Tamil for Tamil Nadu, Odia for Odisha, Kannada for Karnataka, Malayalam for Kerala, Punjabi for Punjab, Bengali for West Bengal, Hindi/Urdu for UP). Candidates who cannot produce acceptable proof of having studied the specified local language in 10th or 12th standard must qualify the LPT. Failing the required LPT will result in disqualification.

faqs.question: Will applying outside your home state automatically cause LPT problems?
faqs.answer: No. Your home state is not the deciding factor. The important question is whether you can prove/meet the language requirement of the state applied for. A candidate from Delhi could apply for Maharashtra, but if they cannot establish Marathi proficiency through standard qualification routes, they may have to take the LPT. Do not choose a state simply because it has a lower cutoff.

faqs.question: If I apply for SBI Clerk from another state, where will my exam centre be?
faqs.answer: You can generally appear for the Preliminary and Mains examination at a notified examination centre of your choice/availability, subject to SBI's arrangements. However, your recruitment is against the state applied for. SBI's rules state that the local-language test (LPT) is conducted at a centre decided by SBI in the state applied for, at the candidate's own expense. (Exam centre ≠ state of recruitment).

faqs.question: How should candidates choose a state when applying for SBI Clerk?
faqs.answer: Choose the state where you genuinely satisfy the local-language requirement first; then compare vacancies and expected competition. The recommended sequence is: Language eligibility → vacancy → expected competition → posting preference. Remember that candidates are considered against the State/UT applied for and are posted in that state if selected.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Regular and Backlog vacancies in SBI recruitment?
faqs.answer: A Regular vacancy is a newly identified vacancy for the current recruitment cycle. A Backlog vacancy is a reserved vacancy from an earlier recruitment that remained unfilled and is carried forward to be filled through a special drive. The current 1,538-post notification is specifically a backlog recruitment, which explains the unusual state-wise vacancy distribution.

faqs.question: Can eligible candidates apply for both Regular and Backlog SBI Clerk recruitments?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you are eligible for both and SBI permits applications for both drives. They are separate recruitment drives. For example, an eligible SC/ST/OBC candidate could potentially participate in both the backlog recruitment and the upcoming regular recruitment, provided they satisfy the eligibility conditions of both.

faqs.question: Will the exams for SBI Clerk Regular and Backlog recruitments be separate?
faqs.answer: Do not assume they will be combined. The current notification is a separate Special Recruitment Drive, so candidates should treat it as a separate recruitment unless SBI subsequently announces otherwise. Expect separate application and exam processes.

faqs.question: Can General (Unreserved) candidates apply for these SBI Clerk backlog vacancies?
faqs.answer: No. The 1,538 backlog vacancies are reserved exclusively for SC, ST, and OBC candidates carried forward from previous recruitment drives. Unreserved / General category candidates cannot claim an SC/ST/OBC backlog seat.

faqs.question: What is the age limit and cutoff date for SBI Clerk Special Drive 2026?
faqs.answer: For the backlog notification, the basic age requirement is 20 to 28 years as of the cut-off date specified in the official notification, plus applicable relaxations for reserved categories (5 years for SC/ST, 3 years for OBC, up to 10–15 years for PwBD). Ensure you check your exact Date of Birth against the specific cut-off date stated in the notification.

faqs.question: Why are some states showing SC/ST vacancies but zero OBC vacancies?
faqs.answer: Because backlog vacancies are category-specific. If SBI had an SC/ST backlog in a particular state but no OBC backlog, it cannot convert or reassign those seats. A table showing SC: 0 | ST: 12 | OBC: 0 simply reflects historical unfilled reserved positions for that state, not a policy of ignoring OBC candidates.

faqs.question: Is the SBI Clerk 2026 question paper available in English?
faqs.answer: Yes. The examination paper is provided in English along with Hindi and the relevant regional language(s) depending on the state (e.g., English/Hindi/Marathi in Maharashtra, English/Hindi/Gujarati in Gujarat, English/Hindi/Odia in Odisha, English/Hindi/Bengali in WB, English/Hindi/Urdu in UP/Bihar). The question paper medium is separate from the LPT requirement.

faqs.question: Did SBI Apprentice recruitment reduce regular Clerk vacancies?
faqs.answer: No. There is no basis in the official notification to conclude that Apprentice recruitment reduced Clerk vacancies. SBI Apprentice and SBI Junior Associate are different recruitment streams. The 1,538-post announcement is a backlog drive, and the upcoming regular Junior Associate recruitment will provide the actual fresh vacancy numbers.

faqs.question: Why are videos claiming 9,000 to 11,000+ vacancies when this notification says 1,538?
faqs.answer: Because numbers like 9,000 or 11,000+ circulating online represent projected estimates for the upcoming Regular recruitment cycle, whereas 1,538 is the officially notified count for the Special Backlog Drive. faqs.question: Where can candidates download the official SBI Clerk notification PDF?

overview: Ministry of Defence, Civilian Direct Recruitment Board, CHQ, ASC Centre (South) - Bangalore, Post - Agram, Bangalore - 560007 has published a direct recruitment notification in Employment News (15 - 21 August 2026) for filling 62 Group 'C' Civilian posts.

The vacancy includes 24 Fireman, 14 Leading Fireman, 8 Tradesman Mate (Labour), 6 Civilian Motor Driver (OG), 3 Civilian Catering Instructor (CCI), 3 Fire Engine Driver, 2 Cleaner, 1 Cook, and 1 MTS (Chowkidar) posts across various military stations in India.

Eligible Indian citizens (10th Pass / Diploma holders) can apply offline by submitting their application on plain paper in the prescribed format along with self-attested document copies within 21 days from the date of publication in Employment News (Last Date: 05 September 2026).
Selection will be based on Physical / Skill / Trade Test followed by a 150-mark Written Examination.

Endurance Test: Carrying 65.5 kg weight to 183 meters in 96 sec, clearing 2.7m ditch, climbing 3m rope.
Civilian Motor Driver (OG): 10th Pass. Must possess valid driving license for both Heavy and Light Motor Vehicles with minimum 2 years driving experience.
Fire Engine Driver: 10th Pass. At least 3 years driving experience of heavy vehicles with valid driving license. Fireman course certification preferred.

Cook: 10th Pass with knowledge of Indian Cooking and proficiency in trade.

150 Objective MCQs for 150 Marks (2 Hours duration). Bilingual (English & Hindi). 0.25 negative marking per wrong answer.
